lessons.title: Do you exercise in winter?
lessons.description: One Minute English video lesson for Beginner learners.
lessons.transcriptHtml:
Hello, my name is Elizabeth. I am from America. And my question is, do you exercise in winter?

Yes, I exercise in winter. I like to walk my dog. I walk my dog to the park. I walk two hours a day. I do not belong to a gym. I like to exercise by myself. I lift weights at my house. I ride my bike. It is cold outside, but I like to exercise inside. I run outside. I run with my friend on the street. I run twice a week. I like to race, so I need to practice. Yes, I like to exercise in winter. It is not as hot as summer.

My question for you is, do you exercise in winter?

I do not have a zoo in my town. My town is small. It has many animals. It has raccoons, it has squirrels, it has dogs and cats, it has ducks, but it does not have a zoo. lessons.description: One Minute English video lesson for High-Beginner learners.
lessons.transcriptHtml:
Hi everyone, I'm Jill and I'm from Australia. And my question today is what did you do over the weekend?

So last weekend I actually had a very special weekend. I took my mom on a trip to Tedra Island. We took a boat down to Tedra Island and we spent the whole weekend going on lots of big walks and eating lots of really good seafood. We ate lots of abalone and lots of sashimi, which was super fresh and delicious. And we went on lots of hikes. They have a beautiful mountain in the center of the island and all around it is big forest. And so we hiked through the forest and we saw lots of beautiful colors that are happening right now because it is autumn.

In Korea, we also went to a massage shop where we were able to sleep a little and have massages, and we drank lots and lots of good coffee, which was surprising because I wasn't expecting that we had really good weather, which was very lucky because it can be a little bit cold. But yeah, I had a really lovely weekend.

And what about you? What did you do over the weekend?

On Thursday evening, we often play board games with my family. On Friday morning, I teach English again, and on Friday afternoon I go to the park or I visit my mother. On Saturday, I often meet with a friend, usually in the afternoon to drink coffee. Sometimes on Saturday night I go to see a play and on Sunday we go to the park or we go to the gym.

lessons.title: What are monthly events in your area?
lessons.description: One Minute English video lesson for High-Beginner learners.
lessons.transcriptHtml:
Hi, I'm Elise, and I'm going to talk about the weather and festivities in Peru.

In January, it's summer and lots of people go to the beach at the coast. Children are on summer holiday. In February, they celebrate carnival by throwing lots of water balloons at each other. In March, children go back to school. In April, they celebrate Easter with some really delicious special breads. In May, lots of tourists start coming to Peru, and it's quite cold because it's almost winter.

In June, there are a lot of religious festivities. One of the most important ones is called in Inti Raymi, and this happens in Cusco. In July, they celebrate Independence Day at the end of the month. In August, children have two weeks of holiday again. In September, there aren't many festivities, and winter is almost over.

In October, there's a very important religious festival called Lord of the Miracles. It's biggest in Lima. In November, it starts heating up a little bit, and the rainy season sometimes starts in the mountains and in the jungle, too. In December, it's definitely the rainy season and children start looking forward to their summer holiday.

So whenever I'm working from home, I always like to brew myself a cup of tea. It just makes my day go a little bit better.

So after this, I will probably plan to go for another walk, but right now I'm going to finish up work for the day and that is what I'm doing right now.

So you can't play sports, you can't do exercise. But Korea has some great parks near the river, and the parks near the river are perfect for sports. You can run, you can ride a bike, you can play sports, you can do exercise, you can even lift weights. They have little weight machines down there and you can exercise. They have these all over Korea, actually. So you can definitely get exercise in Korea and you don't have to go to a gym. So the parks in Korea are fantastic, some of the best in the world. You can do so many things in these parks, and that's one of the reasons I really, really love coming to Korea.

lessons.description: One Minute English video lesson for High-Beginner learners.
lessons.transcriptHtml:

My job is a personal trainer. This means I get to help people to lose weight, to get more slim. I get to help people to live a better quality of life because you have a better life when you are more stronger, when you're able to do more things, when you're able to walk further and when you're able to lift things. I also get to help people, to build confidence, to love themselves more.

I really love my job. I love my job so much that I stop my other job to focus on this job. This job is my passion because I love this job.

lessons.title: What did you do last night?
lessons.description: One Minute English video lesson for High-Beginner learners.
lessons.transcriptHtml:
Hi everyone. My name is Jill, and I'm from Australia. And my question today is, what did you do last night?

I had a really fun night last night. I got to meet with some friends that I hadn't seen in a while, so my friend cooked dinner for us, so we went to her place and we sat together, we ate all of the food, and we talked. We laughed and we danced a little all through the night. She made a beautiful dish with mushroom rice and chicken and potatoes, and afterwards we helped clean, so we vacuumed her living room. We cleaned the dishes, and then we decided that we wanted some dessert. And so we walked to the nearest bubble tea shop where we laughed so much that we were scared we were going to get kicked out, but we didn't. And so we sat, we laughed, we talked, and then I had to say goodnight and come home for the evening.

What about you? What did you do last night? Did you do anything fun?

lessons.description: One Minute English video lesson for High-Beginner learners.
lessons.transcriptHtml:
Hi, I am Elise, and I'm going to talk about the difference between living in the city and living in the countryside.

So in the countryside, the cities and villages are smaller than big cities, which means they're calmer. There's less traffic and less pollution. So they are usually considered healthier to live in than living in the big city. But some people do find it less interesting or a bit more boring to live in the countryside because the cities offer more entertainment options. Large cities also offer more options in terms of education and employment, but the crime levels are higher, too. So it's really a personal choice.

lessons.description: One Minute English video lesson for High-Beginner learners.
lessons.transcriptHtml:
Hi, my name is Nerissa and I'm from the Philippines. My question is, what drinks do you dislike?

I dislike coconut juice and beer. Coconut juice tastes weird to me, and I can't eat or drink anything with coconut. I also don't like beer because it's too bitter for me. I don't enjoy it. What about you? What drinks do you dislike?

lessons.title: How was your day?
lessons.description: One Minute English video lesson for High-Beginner learners.
lessons.transcriptHtml:
Hi everyone. This is your teacher, Todd and I will talk about my day.

So today I had a really good day. I woke up early and I read for a bit. I read a book that I love. It's got a really, really good story. And then I took a drive. I drove down here to the countryside and I walked along the rice fields here and I just relaxed.

Then I went to the beach and I sat on the beach and just did nothing. I did nothing. I just sat there and I looked out at the ocean and just cleared my mind. It was a really nice day. So it was a really fun Sunday. I felt relaxed all day and I didn't feel stressed, and now I'm ready for work tomorrow. So, yeah, it was a good day.

  • How about you?
  • What did you do today?
  • Did you drive anywhere?
  • Did you go anywhere?
  • Did you talk to anyone?
  • Did you buy anything today?

I didn't buy anything. Oh wait, I did. I bought lunch, but besides that, I didn't buy anything.

  • So what about you?

lessons.description: One Minute English video lesson for High-Beginner learners.
lessons.transcriptHtml:
Hi. In this video I'm going to talk a little bit about my plans for tonight. So right now I am at a park.

You can kind of see the park here, and I'm going to go running. I'm going to run for about 40 minutes and I am going to get some exercise I really need to run. I try to run one hour every day, and then after I run, I'm going to take some photos of the park because I love this park and I'm going to share them with my friends. I'm going to post on Facebook, and then after that I am going to drive home, and then I'm going to have dinner with my family. I think tonight we're going to have pizza, although I'm not sure. And then after dinner, I think I'm going to relax and chat with my mom and my dad, and then I'm going to go to bed early. I'm not going to stay up late because tomorrow I have to get up early because I'm going to drive to another city and I'm going to meet my niece and nephew because my nephew is getting married. So I'm going to be doing a lot of things, so I'm going to be very busy.

I don't use the bus that much. I have a car, so I drive a lot. But in Thailand, I don't drive at all. I never drive actually. So I either take the bus or I take the BTS. So that's a little bit different. Also in Japan, I don't walk much, don't walk around that much. But in Thailand, I walk around a lot. I walk to the park, I walk down the street. I'm just always walking. So I kind of like that.

In Japan, I speak Japanese, but I don't speak that much. Actually. I don't know why. I guess because people don't talk as much in Japan, and maybe my Japanese is not as good. But in Thailand, I speak Thai a lot, so maybe that's also a little bit different. In Thailand, I don't spend that much money, but Bangkok is getting more expensive. And then where I live in Japan's not too expensive, so I don't spend that much money there, but I spend much more money on rent in Japan than I do in Thailand. So both places are great. I love 'em, but they're just a little bit different.

lessons.title: What are you wearing today?
lessons.description: One Minute English video lesson for Intermediate learners.
lessons.transcriptHtml:
Hi everyone. My name is Jill and I'm from Australia. And my question today is, what are you wearing today?

I'm actually really excited to answer this question because I am wearing my new favorite T-shirt, and it is from my most recent holiday. It is the shade of green that I love the most because it reminds me of the forest, and it says on here, you can either fight it or ride it, and it has a picture of a girl who is riding a wave, which is perfect because on this holiday I went on a surfing camp. I'm also wearing today a necklace that I always wear with me. And this necklace is really special because one thing about me is that I love to travel, and on this necklace are little trinkets, which I have collected from all of my travels. For example, the shell is from Spain. This little glass pendant is from Italy, and this silver key is from India. And I am wearing this today, and I wear this every day because it reminds me of happy memories that I had from when I was traveling.

What about you? What are you wearing today?

And do they hold any special meaning to you?

trinkets

Meaning: Small decorative objects that are not very expensive.

Examples:

  1. She wears trinkets she bought while traveling.
  2. The market was full of colorful trinkets.

necklace

Meaning: A piece of jewelry worn around the neck.

Examples:

  1. She wears a necklace every day.
  2. His gift to her was a gold necklace.

shade

Meaning: A particular type or degree of a color.

Examples:

  1. Her shirt is a shade of green she loves the most.
  2. That shade of blue looks great on you.

riding a wave

Meaning: Standing or lying on a surfboard and moving on top of a wave.

Examples:

  1. The picture shows a girl riding a wave.
  2. He learned how to ride a wave at surfing camp.

pendant

Meaning: A small decorative object hanging from a necklace.

Examples:

  1. The pendant on her necklace is made of glass.
  2. He gave her a silver pendant from Italy.

hold special meaning

Meaning: To be personally important or emotionally valuable.

Examples:

  1. These trinkets hold special meaning from my travels.
  2. The ring holds special meaning because it was a gift.

lessons.title: Is trash recycled in your country?
lessons.description: One Minute English video lesson for Intermediate learners.
lessons.transcriptHtml:
Hide / Show Transcript

Hi, my name is Sarah. I come from England, and my question is, is trash recycled in your country?

So the answer to that is yes. We definitely do recycle in England. It is starting to thankfully get a lot more serious and, you know, people are really starting to recycle more, especially since now, I think that you can be fined quite a lot of money if you don't recycle properly in the U.K. As of now, I think we have three different types of trash that mainly get recycled: plastic, glass, and cardboard, I believe are the three different things that we recycle right now.

We also have, like, three different trash cans, which are different colors to help you remember which type of trash goes into which type of trash can. And yeah, then the garbage guy will come and collect it, take it away, and they are separated, which makes it easier to recycle and to better help the environment.

So yeah, we definitely do recycle in England.
lessons.vocabularyHtml:
since

Meaning: From a time in the past until now; because.

Examples:

  1. People recycle more since new rules started.
  2. I’ve lived here since 2010.

thankfully

Meaning: Happily or luckily; used when something good has happened.

Examples:

  1. Thankfully, people are recycling more now.
  2. Thankfully, it didn’t rain during the cleanup.

definitely

Meaning: Certainly; without any doubt.

Examples:

  1. We definitely recycle in England.
  2. I definitely agree with you.

cardboard

Meaning: Thick, stiff paper used to make boxes.

Examples:

  1. We recycle cardboard with paper and boxes.
  2. The package was made of cardboard.

fined

Meaning: Made to pay money as a punishment.

Examples:

  1. You can be fined if you don’t recycle properly.
  2. He was fined for parking in the wrong place.

properly

Meaning: In the right or correct way.

Examples:

  1. Please recycle properly by using the right bin.
  2. The machine didn’t work properly.

lessons.title: What did you do last night?
lessons.description: One Minute English video lesson for Intermediate learners.
lessons.transcriptHtml:
Hi everyone. My name is Jill and I'm from Australia. And my question today is, what did you do last night?

I had a really fun night last night. I got to meet with some friends that I hadn't seen in a while, so my friend cooked dinner for us, and so we went to her place and we sat together, we ate all of the food, and we talked, we laughed and we danced a little all through the night. She made a beautiful dish with mushroom rice and chicken and potatoes, and afterwards we helped clean, so we vacuumed her living room. We cleaned the dishes, and then we decided that we wanted some dessert. And so we walked to the nearest bubble tea shop where we laughed so much that we were scared we were going to get kicked out, but we didn't. And so we sat, we laughed, we talked, and then I had to say goodnight and come home for the evening.

What about you? What did you do last night? Did you do anything fun?
lessons.vocabularyHtml:
vacuumed

Meaning: Cleaned the floor using a machine that sucks up dust and dirt.

Examples:

  1. We vacuumed the living room after dinner.
  2. She vacuumed her house before the guests arrived.

all through the night

Meaning: For the entire night; from evening until morning.

Examples:

  1. We talked and danced all through the night.
  2. It rained all through the night.

afterwards

Meaning: After something has happened; later.

Examples:

  1. We cleaned the kitchen afterwards.
  2. Afterwards, we went out for dessert.

get kicked out

Meaning: To be forced to leave a place because of bad behavior or breaking rules.

Examples:

  1. They laughed so much they almost got kicked out of the café.
  2. He got kicked out of class for being noisy.

bubble tea

Meaning: A sweet drink with milk or fruit flavor and small chewy balls called tapioca pearls.

Examples:

  1. We went to a bubble tea shop after dinner.
  2. She ordered a large bubble tea with brown sugar pearls.

in a while

Meaning: For a long time; recently not.

Examples:

  1. I hadn’t seen my friends in a while.
  2. We haven’t eaten out in a while.

lessons.description: One Minute English video lesson for Intermediate learners.

Hi. My name is Nev, and I'm from Canada. My question for today is do you belong to a group or community?

If I were to become one, and hopefully I will in the future, I would like to join communities that help people around us, communities that offer services for let's say homeless people or people who are struggling when it comes to their mental health or things like that. So I think it would be great to give something back to the community and to be a part of something useful.

lessons.title: What do you usually eat for dinner?
lessons.description: One Minute English video lesson for Intermediate learners.
lessons.transcriptHtml:
Hide / Show Transcript

Hello. My name is Lilith and I'm from Armenia. Today, my question is, what do you usually eat for dinner?

Here in Armenia, we have lots of traditional dishes which are made with meat and are really delicious, but somehow I happen not to like them. It's probably because all my childhood I've eaten Armenian traditional food, and I have grown to dislike this kind of food.

So now that I'm lucky to be living alone, I can cook whatever I like. I'm really fond of Italian food. So for dinner, I usually have either a pasta with some different types of sauce, or some soup, sometimes mashed potatoes with steak, and occasionally pizza. I really like seafood and fish. So from time to time, I make some new dishes which include seafood, or fried fish, or fish and chips, and things like that.

lessons.title: How often do you use public tranportation?
lessons.description: One Minute English video lesson for Intermediate learners.
lessons.transcriptHtml:
Hide / Show Transcript

How often do I use public transport?

Pretty much never these days. I recently moved to New Orleans, as we pronounce it here, New Orleans. New Orleans, Louisiana: NOLA.

There's very limited public transport in New Orleans. There's a great street car, a tram, as I would call it. But I'm more of a walker. I love walking. If something's close enough, I'll walk there. And having recently had a baby and things being quite far away in New Orleans, we had to buy a car. I haven't driven a car since I was in Japan about 10 years ago. But a car is kind of essential here.

When I'm in other cities, I do like to walk, or get public transportation. I love trains and long distance buses, but unfortunately reality nowadays means that in a big city like New Orleans, I need to drive a car. So I do.

The question that I'm answering is, is what are the best and worst parts of your job?

Currently, the main job that I do is provide voiceovers, and whether that be for YouTube videos or commercials, I provide the voice behind it.

So, one of the best parts of this job is that having so many scripts to narrate for different channels, I get to learn a lot. I've learnt about the facts about space. The worst part about this is sometimes not being able to pronounce names and places properly. Because my main language is English, if I get a place or a name that's German or Russian or from Cambodia, I find it very difficult to pronounce, and I often have to go onto YouTube or go onto the internet to find out how to pronounce it correctly.

lessons.description: One Minute English video lesson for Intermediate learners.

Hi. My name is Nev and I come from Canada. For today my question is would you like to have a dangerous job?

To be honest, this is an easy question, and my answer is no. I wouldn't like to have a dangerous job. I work as a kindergarten teacher, and to be honest, I love my job. So, if I were to change it, I still wouldn't consider doing anything that's dangerous to me or people around me.

Why?

That would be an interesting thing to explain. Maybe because I think I wouldn't be able to do such a job because I'm very sensitive, and if I see someone in pain or in any kind of trouble that could potentially seriously hurt or damage him, I don't think I would be able to deal with all that on a daily basis. And job is something that you do every day so we might as well like it. That's why I'm keeping mine.

What about you? Would you consider changing your job and having a dangerous one?

lessons.description: One Minute English video lesson for Intermediate learners.
lessons.transcriptHtml:
Hide / Show Transcript

Hello. My name is Veronica, and I'm from the United States. My question today is what colors do you like and dislike to wear?

Obviously, one of the colors that I like to wear is blue. I think it's my favorite color to wear because I feel like it suits my skin tone very well. Since I have a lighter skin tone and darker hair, I feel like blue looks very good on me. Sometimes I wear a muted blue like I am today. Sometimes I wear a very bright, like a royal blue. Either one of those I think really looks nice on me, and so it is actually my favorite color to wear.

My least favorite color to wear is yellow. You won't find a lot of yellow in my wardrobe. And the only reason is I think yellow is a beautiful color. It is bright. It is captivating and it looks so good on so many people. I just don't feel like yellow looks good on me. So it is very rare that you will ever see me wearing the color yellow.

lessons.title: What do you usually eat for lunch?
lessons.description: One Minute English video lesson for Intermediate learners.
lessons.transcriptHtml:
Hide / Show Transcript

Hello. My name is Veronica, and I'm from the United States. And my question today is, what do you usually eat for lunch?

Well, get ready because my answer might be a little bit boring for you. I usually eat the same thing for lunch every day, and it's normally a salad. And the reason why I eat the same thing for lunch every day is because it's a lot easier to do that, plus, I try to have a healthier lifestyle.

So for me, if I'm eating a salad at lunch every day, I know that I'm getting the amount of vegetables and fruits that I need throughout my day, plus I don't have a lot of time to sit down and actually eat a big meal, so for me if I'm able to stop and have something healthy and refreshing, it's not going to slow me down. I know that there are a lot of cultures that believe in eating a big meal at lunch. But if I were to eat, say for example, a big steak and a potato, I would need a nap right afterwards, so normally I just have a salad for lunch every day so that I can stay healthy and keep going.

Hi, my name is Nev and I come from Canada. My question for today is, what are your beauty secrets?

Okay. So as you can see, I'm not wearing any makeup right now. And that's what I try to do every day, to go makeup-free and allow myself and my skin to breathe. Apart from washing my face, I apply a moisturizer or a serum daily, and that's pretty much it. Every now and then I put on a facial mask. And like I said, I try to keep it simple. I try not to put on too many products that would eventually hurt my skin.

Hello, my name is Lilit, and I'm from Armenia. Today, my question is, what is a fun party that you attended?

For me, a fun party that I've attended recently was my friend's 25th birthday. We rented a lovely house in the countryside, and about 10 or 12 friends were invited to the party. And we went there by car.

Although we didn't stay the night, we had a really great day. There was a really large garden with lots of fruit trees and pavilions and a place to play some games. And there was a large pool where we swam all morning and we sunbathed. And then in the evening we made barbecue. We also had lots of pizza and all sorts of junk food, which I really love by the way. And then in the evening, we played some card games, some board games together, and it was lots of fun. We had music playing on the speakers really loudly, and we were lucky because there weren't any neighbors around. So there was no one to complain about the noise. So yeah, I really enjoyed this party.

lessons.description: One Minute English video lesson for Intermediate learners.
lessons.transcriptHtml:
Hide / Show Transcript

Hello, my name's Elaine, and I'm from England. My question was, do you like to make your own clothes?

I wish I could make my own clothes. I have tried, but I don't have the patience. My mom's actually a costume designer, and so when I was little she used to make all my clothes for me. I had lots of beautiful party dresses and nobody else had anything like them. In fact, my mom even bought me a sewing machine for my birthday last year. I haven't had much time to learn how to use it.

I really like buying vintage clothes or secondhand clothes and adjusting them. So I will try to, for example, if a dress is too long, I will try to take it up. Or if something is too wide, I will try to take it in. Maybe sometimes I like to change a button or to make it more beautiful. I find this is also an ecological way of shopping. It's a bit unusual, and I don't want to dress like everyone else.

But what about you? Do you make your own clothes? Do you modernize or revamp your clothes? Let us know.

If you could change your nationality, what nationality would you be?

I would definitely choose to be Italian. First of all, because I've been speaking Italian my whole life, since I was a toddler, so that would be pretty easy for me. lessons.title: What was your most embarrassing moment?
lessons.description: One Minute English video lesson for Intermediate learners.
lessons.transcriptHtml:
Hello, my name is Preah, and I am from Belize. My question is, what was your most embarrassing moment?

So when I was 18 years old, I decided that I wanted to move to Mexico. I was an adult, and I felt like I could do anything I wanted. I also thought that I knew Spanish, but I quickly learned that I didn't know as much as I thought. So I was at this mall and there was this man. He was doing a play, and he wanted to invite me on stage as a part of his play.

And I kept telling him in Spanish, "Soy embarazado. Soy embarazado."

And I thought that I was saying, "I'm embarrassed" because "embarazado - embarrassed" I thought they meant the same thing.

And he kept telling me, "congratulations, congratulations."

And I was like, "no, soy embarazado."

And he kept saying, "congratulations, boy or girl?"

And I was like, "I am a girl," I told him.

It wasn't until afterwards I realized, or I learned that "embarazado" or "embarazada" meant pregnant and embarrassed, what I actually wanted to say, meant "avergonzado," right?

So that was pretty embarrassing because everyone thought that I was pregnant, but I actually wanted to say that I was embarrassed.

lessons.description: One Minute English video lesson for Intermediate learners.
lessons.transcriptHtml:
Hi. I'm Ozlem and I'm from Turkey. My question is, what do you like about your country?

I love many things about my country. Firstly, it is located in a unique geographical position. It is a bridge between Asia and Europe. It is one of the world's top 10 travel destinations, and there are many reasons for this. For example, every region in Turkey has its own kitchen culture. So be sure to gain weight if you come here.

And apart from big cities like Ankara, Istanbul or Izmir, there are plenty of nature escapes. And then, what else?

It has beautiful beaches because it is surrounded by Black Sea, Aegean Sea and Mediterranean. They are all great. There are many, many other things I can talk about it, but it would take hours for me, so I strongly suggest you visit here. Bye!

My name is Rachel and I'm from Australia. And my question is, do you always eat healthy food?

No. I love chocolate. I have it once a day. Not a lot, but a little bit. I love sweet things. I have a sweet tooth, so. I also do try and eat healthy. You don't have to just stick to only, only healthy.

That's my opinion, at least.

lessons.title: Will there still be language schools in 10 years?
lessons.description: One Minute English video lesson for Intermediate learners.
lessons.transcriptHtml:
Hi, I'm Ozlem and I'm from Turkey. Here is my question. Will there still be language schools in 10 years?

No, I don't think there will be language schools in 10 years' time. Traditionally, language lessons took place in a classroom, students at their desks and teachers at the front, but this has changed a great deal, hasn't it? I mean, with the COVID in our lives, now we got used to teaching and learning online. And there are new learning management systems that bring teachers and students together. And the teachers keep track of their students, they can send materials from those systems as well.

And secondly, there are also many great apps for a language learner. You can find many apps out there. And thirdly, you can also had a private tutor. You can have your private tutor. You can have your lessons, however and whenever you like. So, see you.

lessons.title: How has your life changed in the last five years?
lessons.description: One Minute English video lesson for Intermediate learners.
lessons.transcriptHtml:
Hello, my name is Preah. I am from Belize and I am an ESL teacher. Belize is in Central America. It is actually the only English speaking country in Central America. And my question was how has your life changed in the last five years?

And I'm glad I got this question because two days ago I was thinking about this exact same thing. I am 21 years old, will be 22 in November. So five years ago I was actually graduating high school. Yes, I am a 2017 graduate and since then I have traveled. I have a 2-year-old daughter. I have lived in three different and three different locations in my country. So I've moved around a bit and I am now a teacher myself. So in five years I would say a lot has happened. I am going to school, I'm about to graduate university in one year, and I have met thousands and thousands of people that are from all around the world have a lot of knowledge from traveling experiences that I never would've had if I had just stayed in my hometown. So those are the different changes.

lessons.title: How do you feel about having a pet?
lessons.description: One Minute English video lesson for Intermediate learners.
lessons.transcriptHtml:
Hi, I'm Ozlem, and I'm from Turkey. Here is my question: How do you feel about having a pet?

Having a pet brings a circle of love into our lives. This is certain, and I remember reading an article about human and animal connection, and in that article, there were around ten health benefits, like lower depression, blood rates, more physical activity, and so on. Yes, they are definitely good for humans.

And actually, I have a pet, and we took him when he was a puppy, and he really brought lots of love to our lives, lots of joy to our lives. We all love him very much, and we try to spend time with him. But on the contrary, I sometimes feel guilty about him because I cannot spend so much time with him, so that makes me sad.

Yes, as a result, having a pet is definitely good for humans. But the question is, are we good for them?

Thank you. See you.

lessons.transcriptHtml:

He was the president in the 1860s, and the reason why I think President Lincoln is my favorite historical figure is that he freed the slaves and he especially freed the black people in America. And he was a forefather for everybody who wants to have equality and civil rights and freedom for everybody.

Okay, so is your favorite historical figure. Please do tell.

lessons.title: Have you ever tried a fad diet?
lessons.description: One Minute English video lesson for Intermediate learners.
lessons.transcriptHtml:
Have I ever had a fad diet?

No, I have never had any type of diet. Okay. Why haven't I had a fad diet?

First, it's because it is a trendy weight loss plan, and I don't usually follow trends. Second, it's because I think I'm already fit in my body. I don't think that I need to be losing weight. I don't think that I need to be following any type of diet for the moment. Okay. Maybe in the future if I ever gain weight, I would do it, although I don't think so because I don't like these things. That diet is a very, very severe diet. I don't like these things. Am I against it, though? No. Everybody's free to do whatever they want with their body. I'm nobody to judge, but for me, I don't think I would ever do it even if I gained weight, but maybe one day, I don't know.

Who knows? So, yeah, that's it.

lessons.title: What is your favorite meal?
lessons.description: One Minute English video lesson for Intermediate learners.
lessons.transcriptHtml:
Hello, my name is Juan Cruz. I'm from Argentina. And my question is, what is your favorite meal?

Well, so my favorite meal is typical here in Argentina. It's called empanadas, and my favorite type of empanadas are meat empanadas. So my family owned a pizza shop when I was little, and I would have them all the time. So, when I have them now, it's like going back to when I was a kid. So it consists of making a filling, which has meat in it, and you put that in a dough. The dough can then go fried or in the oven, which is my preference for about, I think, half an hour, 45 minutes. And then when you eat it, you can add a little bit of sugar to it to have a salty and sugary taste in it.

And I absolutely love them.

lessons.title: What do you think is the most difficult language to learn?
lessons.description: One Minute English video lesson for Intermediate learners.
lessons.transcriptHtml:
Hello, my name is Preah. The question I was asked was, what do you think is the most difficult language to learn?

And as you probably know, English is the most difficult to learn, and that is coming from an English teacher. Okay, now, why do I say this? I know how to speak four languages: English, Spanish, Creole, which is my native language, my country's native language, patois is English, patois, as well as American, I'm just kidding. American isn't a language. But yeah, I know how to speak English, Spanish, and what we call Creole. But why do I say English? It's because there's a lot of terms. There's a lot of different tenses. There's a lot of words that mean one thing, but it's pronounced a different way. There's a lot of letters that are silent in words. There's a lot of different pronunciations for letters, and it's also very different than what other countries or other languages are used to.

So that is why I would say English is the most difficult.

lessons.title: What do you usually eat for dinner?
lessons.description: One Minute English video lesson for Intermediate learners.
lessons.transcriptHtml:
What do I usually eat for dinner?

Okay, so every day is different. There isn't that one kind of food that I usually eat or that one dish that I always eat. No, every day is different. Sometimes I eat fish soup. Sometimes I eat vegetable soup, sometimes noodles, sometimes spaghetti. So every day is different. But if you ask me what do I love to eat or what do I prefer, I would say cheese and chicken. Oh my God! Anything that has cheese and chicken in it, I would die for it. Although I'm trying to be vegan. I want to be vegan, but I can't. I love chicken a lot. Oh my God! Anything that has chicken and cheese in it, I would die for it.

  2. Although I like pizza, I prefer pasta.

Examples:

lessons.title: Did you have a part-time job when you were younger?
lessons.description: One Minute English video lesson for Intermediate learners.
lessons.transcriptHtml:
The question that I'm answering is did you have a part-time job when you were younger?

The answer to this is I've had a few part-time jobs, but I'll talk about my first part-time job, which is delivering the newspaper. So, in 1994, when I was still in high school, every Wednesday, I would take a whole stack of newspapers in a trolley and go around the neighborhood and put all these newspapers into people's letter box. Now, it's the local paper, and unfortunately now, the local paper doesn't exist anymore, but I do have those memories when I had to walk around in the rain, had to walk around in the hail, had to walk around in the sunshine on those hot 30 degree days to deliver these newspapers after school without fail.

So, that is my first part-time job.

lessons.title: What is something you loved to do as a child?
lessons.description: One Minute English video lesson for Intermediate learners.
lessons.transcriptHtml:
Hi. My name's Rachel and I'm from Australia, and my question is, what is something you loved to do as a child?

When I was a child I grew up near a gorge. A gorge is kind of like a forest. So I would go for walks. I would ride bikes. I was a very active child. We didn't have phones the way we have phones now, which I'm grateful for. I loved it. I sound old saying that, but yeah, I would play outside, water bombing, playing games with my friends, looking at nature, kangaroos. Where I grew up we had a lot of animals, so it was just exploring and it was a lot of fun.

lessons.title: Who do you speak English with?
lessons.description: One Minute English video lesson for Intermediate learners.
lessons.transcriptHtml:
Hi. I'm Ozlem and I'm from Turkey. Here is my question: Who do you speak English with?

I work as an ESL teacher in a private school here in Turkey. At school, as a general rule, we do not speak our native language because we believe our students should be surrounded by the second language they learn, which is English in our case. So, we try to speak English everywhere anytime we are with them. In the process of language learning, there are four skills students should acquire: Reading, writing, listening, and speaking, and speaking is the productive skill. This means if students, if they need to improve this skill, they need to produce.

Anyway, apart from that, I have many other colleagues and native friends, so we always speak English together. But if you do not have people around you speaking English, you can also find friends online or you can have an English tutor to practice online. That's it. Thank you and see you. Bye.

Examples:

lessons.title: Have you ever taken a road trip before?
lessons.description: One Minute English video lesson for Intermediate learners.
lessons.transcriptHtml:
Hi, I'm Preah. I'm from Belize. I am an ESL teacher. My question was, have you ever taken a road trip before?

I have taken many road trips before, and actually two weeks ago, on the 7th of October, my family and I, we took an eight-hour road trip to Cancun, Mexico. We stopped at a lot of shabby gas stations. We met a lot of amazing and friendly people. Even at the border, we ate some delicious Mexican tacos and tortas, and we had an amazing time in Cancun as well. On our way back. We were actually blocked on the road by two animals: an alligator and a tapir, which is my country's national animal. So, it was very fascinating to see that in Cancun. There was a lot of sightseeing to do. We saw different amusement parks on the way. We stopped in Tulum, Playa del Carmen, as well as Bacalar. All in all, I do hope my family ... (the video cuts off)

lessons.title: Have you ever had a beloved pet?
lessons.description: One Minute English video lesson for Intermediate learners.
lessons.transcriptHtml:
Have you ever had a beloved pet?

I've actually always been a dog person and I've always wanted a dog, but I never really got one up until now. So now I have, I would like to say small puppy, but he is not that small. He's Belgian Shepherd, a Malinois, and he's becoming very big, which is an increasing problem in our household.

But to be honest with you, I never really understood people who had pets, and I never understood how they could love a pet so much. But now that I have him, his name is Maki, by the way, like the sushi. Now that I have Maki in my life, I can definitely understand that you can love an animal so, so much. And if it was up to me, I would spend all of my waking hours with him, but I can't. So I just have to be at peace with that. But yeah, he is a very, very beloved dog in our house.

Examples:

  1. By the way, did you hear about the new restaurant opening downtown?
  2. I met Sarah yesterday, by the way, she asked about you.

Examples:

Examples:

Examples:

Examples:

  2. She had never traveled abroad up until she went to Italy.

Examples:

  1. There are five people in my household.
  2. In our household, everyone helps with the chores.

Examples:

  2. He’s a dog person, but his wife prefers cats.

lessons.title: Do you have a car?
lessons.description: One Minute English video lesson for Intermediate learners.
lessons.transcriptHtml:
Hello everybody. This is Antti from Finland. I'm from Central Finland. My question for elllo.org today is, do you have a car?

And my answer is, yes, I do. I do have a car, and my car is a Hyundai I-20. It's blue, and I need to drive my car every day cause I need to go to school by car. And my school is about 15 kilometers from my home, and there are no bus connections from my home to my school. I also have a bike, and I ride my bike only in summer, and it's more like a hobby.

So what about you?

Do you have a car or would you like to have a car or do you have a bike?

Okay, bye-bye.

lessons.description: One Minute English video lesson for Intermediate learners.
lessons.transcriptHtml:
Hi, my name's Rachel, and I'm from Australia. My question is, is it important for you to have a car?

So, where I live at the moment, there is a lot of public transport, so having a car is not a huge thing for me. Obviously, it would be nice if I had the option to drive around, could be a bit easier, but no. Overall, as long as I have good public transport, it doesn't affect my life that much, and it's actually better for the environment, so I'm okay with it.

lessons.title: What are some tips in language learning?
lessons.description: One Minute English video lesson for Intermediate learners.
lessons.transcriptHtml:
Hi, I'm Ozlem. I'm from Turkey. And here is my question: what are some tips in language learning?

I have been an ESL teacher for over 20 years, and I would like to say a few things about language learning. I always see people trying to find a shortcut in language learning. Yes, you can have a shortcut in the sense of time, but I don't believe you can have a shortcut in the sense of effort. So, number one, you should find the reason: why do you want to learn this language? For example, if you want to speak fluently, you should focus on speaking and listening activities. I generally see people complaining about the amount of time they have spent and have no result at the end. But when we look closer at their studies, we see that they have not spent enough time in that specific skill they want. And secondly, you should follow a system. If you follow a system, if you have a system, and thirdly, if you have fun, this is very important, you will definitely learn the language. So have a system and have fun. Love what you are doing. Thank you. See you later. Bye.

Hello, my name is Veronica, and I'm from the United States. And my question today is have you ever had a makeover?

I have never had a makeover, but now that I'm answering this question, I feel like that would be a lot of fun. I've actually had this same hairstyle for several years now, so I think a makeover would actually be really cool.

But even though I have not had a makeover, I've seen plenty of TV shows where they do makeovers on people, and I think it is fascinating, especially when you see a person who has made big changes in their life. For example, if someone lost a lot of weight and then suddenly they came in and gave them a makeover with a new hairstyle and perhaps new makeup and teach them how to wear brand new clothes now that their body is completely different. I love seeing the expression on the person's face after their makeover, because they're so happy, and the way that they feel on the inside matches how they look on the outside now, both absolutely beautiful. So even though I've never personally had a makeover, I think that they're really incredible.

Hello, everyone. My name is Gian, and I'm from Brazil. And my question right now is what are some tips to learning a language?

Well, I am fluent in three languages. Portuguese from Brazil, English, and Italian. Also, we speak advance level French and Spanish. And I know basics in Mandarin, Chinese and German as well. I would love to learn Russian and Arabic one day as well. So I love languages. I think languages are such a beautiful way to understand more of a culture, and also just expand your internal vocabulary and universe. My best tips will be, definitely be in contact with the language as much as possible.

If you don't have the opportunity to travel to the country that speak that language, just do classes, lessons, try to talk to native people, watch films, games, and practice as much, either with classes or apps or anything you have at your disposal. And of course, the number one thing would be to just travel to a country, and immerse yourself there. Best, if no one speaks any language that you know. So you were forced to communicate in that language. It's scary at first, but I promise you, it will pay off. All right, guys. I'll see you guys next time. Bye-bye.

lessons.transcriptHtml:
Hide / Show Transcript

Hi, my name is Eulices and I'm from Costa Rica. My question is what are some tips to learning a language?

I have three tips for learning a language. The first one is that you need to like this language. There has to be a reason for you to learn so that you have the motivation to continue and to do so. For example, if it allows you to meet new people or it allows you to get a job, or if you like the way it sounds or it's written, that will give you motivation when it gets hard, and generally, it always gets hard because all languages have some kind of barrier.

The second one is that you need to surround yourself with material that is in this language. For example, movies or music, or talking to people who are native to this language, so that you are in constant contact with this language.

And the third one is that you need to practice, because even if you have completely learned a language, which is not something that generally can happen because there is always something new to learn, but even when you have a high level of it, if you don't practice, you will lose it and you will not even notice when you're losing it. So those are my three tips to learning a language.

The question I'm answering today is are you part of a group or community?

Now, the group that I'm part of is a business owners meetup group. So what happens at this group is that once a month, or sometimes once a fortnight, business owners get together, have a cup of coffee at a cafe and discuss the many aspects of owning a business. So whether it's sharing tools, sharing useful websites with each other, or even encouraging another business that might be going through a hard time, that other people also understand what they're going through. There's also an opportunity to celebrate some of the successes people have had in business and also to network and introduce services and products to each other in businesses. It's a fantastic group to be part of. And that's because I've always been in business, and I benefit a lot being in this business meetup group.

lessons.title: Are tattoos frowned upon in your community?
lessons.description: One Minute English video lesson for High-Intermediate learners.
lessons.transcriptHtml:
Hide / Show Transcript

Hello, my name is Veronica, and I'm from the United States. My question today is, are tattoos frowned upon in your community?

I don't believe that tattoos are frowned upon in my community. As a matter of fact, I believe that tattoos have become even more accepted as the years go by. Remember back in the day, it used to be that people with tattoos were looked at as maybe somebody that had been in jail or somebody who was in trouble, or maybe even the biker. You know, tattoos always had kind of a negative connotation, but now a lot of people have tattoos and they see it as something that is artistic.

They treat their body like a canvas, and they're very proud of their tattoos. You see a lot of tattoos, especially within the creative community. People who have jobs that require creativity, but even people who work in regular jobs now. They used to make them wear long sleeves or cover up and now I believe a lot of companies and a lot of communities are more accepting of tattoos because they're starting to see that they're more common and they've become more acceptable.

lessons.title: What is considered taboo in my country?
lessons.description: One Minute English video lesson for High-Intermediate learners.
lessons.transcriptHtml:
Hide / Show Transcript

Hello everyone, my name is Gian, and I'm from Brazil. My question right now is, what is taboo in my country?

Oh, I love this question so much. I am very always interested in knowing little things about different cultures like this. There are so many I can think of, off top of my head. Nothing is, like, that big that people would be extremely offended that I think, or you know, is like super superstitious.

Brazil is a very big and diverse country from, you know, cultures from all over the world, from Europeans to Africans, even Japanese in there, so all those things kind of mix up in a very big melting pot of culture and taboos. But the first thing that came to my mind, funny enough, is it's kind of considered rude to arrive either early or right at the time at a dinner party, for example.

Often in Brazil when you say dinner is at nine and you're going to a friend's house, it's customary to be like, you know, 20 minutes, half an hour late, it's customary, not too late but definitely not too early, for some reason, so that's the first and funniest taboo I can think of about Brazilian culture. I hope to see you guys next time. Bye-bye.

  2. India is known as a diverse country with many languages and traditions.

lessons.title: Do you prefer large or small weddings?
lessons.description: One Minute English video lesson for High-Intermediate learners.
lessons.transcriptHtml:
Hide / Show Transcript

The question that I'm answering is, do you prefer large weddings or small weddings?

Personally, I think every wedding is enjoyable, but the large weddings are much more enjoyable than the small weddings. This is my personal opinion. And let me tell you why. I enjoy going to see the wedding itself, but also love to be part of the crowd during the party. And if the dance floor is full, or if there are a lot of people having a great time laughing, that adds to the atmosphere of the event, and that makes it very enjoyable for me.

For my wedding, I had 210 people attend, and I knew half of them. So for me, it was a great big party. Now, I consider 200 plus a large wedding. Maybe you might find that different, but for me, that size and above are the weddings that I enjoy most.

Hide / Show Transcript

Hi, my name is Thaer, and I am from Jordan. Today's question is what is the best age to get married?

Well, in my opinion, I think there is no certain age to get married in. I mean, the answer to that question would be, are you ready to have a partner for the rest of your life? Because marriage is all about having the best partner to stay for the rest of your life. So, this is, this is in my opinion. But in Jordan, actually, what I think the best age is from 30 to 33 years old because actually, Jordan is considered one of the most expensive countries in the world. So in order to have a, to be settled and to have a good things that you have achieved in life, you need to be about that age to get married. And actually, it's also to get enough of your single life and to move on to the next type of life, which is getting married. So, that's what I think.

So, what do you think, what is the best age to get married?

Hi, my name is Eullices, and I'm from Costa Rica. My question is, what types of TV shows do you like and dislike?

I like science documentaries and crime shows a lot even when they are police dramas because those are the kind of shows that are always showing you something interesting, and you can learn a lot from documentaries, especially if they are scientific. And I do not like dramas when they are just dramas. When they are police dramas or historical or political dramas, they tend to be very interesting. But when they are just about people and relationships, and they spend a lot of time in mellow dramatic scenes or crying a lot, that is not something that regularly holds my interest. So those are the kind of shows that I don't regularly see. But when they are interesting mixes, I give them a shot.

lessons.description: One Minute English video lesson for High-Intermediate learners.
lessons.transcriptHtml:
Hide / Show Transcript

Hello. My name is Lilit, and I'm from Armenia. My question is, what is your idea for a movie?

At some point in our lives, we've all come up with a plot, which we think would be fantastic for a movie. And my idea is for a horror movie, which I think would be called suspense.

So it wouldn't really be a horror movie because there won't be much going on in the movie. However, there will constantly be background music which will lead to people thinking and anticipating that something bad is going to happen, when in reality there will not be anything.

So there will be spooky music which will just intensify the feeling of suspense and shock. But then, the movie will just end like that without anything happening. lessons.description: One Minute English video lesson for High-Intermediate learners.
lessons.transcriptHtml:
Hide / Show Transcript

Hello, my name is Lillit. I'm from Armenia. Today my question is, would you volunteer for medical experiments?

I think medical experiments are a great way of achieving something in medicine and a person who volunteers, so for medical experiments, can easily earn some money.

However, I would not like to volunteer in a medical experiment because I consider myself to be an unlucky person. And if there is even a 1% chance of something going wrong, then I think it will definitely happen to me. Other than that, I'm really afraid of hospitals. And every time I have to go in for a medical checkup or to give some blood tests, I really feel anxious. And I just don't like the environment of the hospitals. So I don't think there is a chance that I would actually volunteer for any medical experiments.

Hello, my name is Nicola and I'm from England. And my question is, would you volunteer for medical experiments?

However, having said that, if I was in a situation where I was quite ill and the treatment that I'd been given hadn't worked, and I had a last resort to volunteer for this new experiment, this new drug, should I say, to volunteer in the experiment, as a last resort, I probably would try . Hi, my name is Nev and I'm from Canada. My question for today is, what odd jobs have you had?

lessons.title: What is an ideal wedding?
lessons.description: One Minute English video lesson for High-Intermediate learners.
lessons.transcriptHtml:
Hide / Show Transcript

Hello, my name is Lilit, I'm from Armenia. Today, my question is what is an ideal wedding?

For me, an ideal wedding includes both traditional and non-traditional elements of a wedding and traditionally, I think a bride should be wearing a white dress and the groom should be wearing a suit. In Armenia, we have this tradition when a groom has to pick up the bride from her home, and I think this moment is really emotional when he sees her for the first time and then together, they go to the church. Going to the church is an important part of Armenian weddings, and I think it's really beautiful.

After that, there is a session for taking photographs in the nature or somewhere beautiful, and then everyone goes to a restaurant to celebrate the wedding. The ideal celebration starts with the groom and the bride having their first dance which is usually a tango or a waltz and after that, it's all just really crazy because everyone's drinking, eating, and there's lots of dancing until everyone is really tired, and they just decide to go home.

lessons.title: What is an ideal wedding?
lessons.description: One Minute English video lesson for High-Intermediate learners.
lessons.transcriptHtml:
Hide / Show Transcript

Hello, my name is Nicola and I'm from England and my question is what is an ideal wedding?

I think that depends on your own personal taste to be honest. Many girls, because I think it's the women that tend to be arranging the weddings rather than the men, but they tend to go for the traditional big, white wedding with the very expensive dress, the very expensive place to eat, to have the reception, the DJ and so on and so on.

Personally, I think that spending tens of thousands of pounds on a wedding is a waste of money. I would prefer something quite simple like a little ceremony with just some close friends and family of course, and then something to eat afterwards and maybe obviously some music to have a little bit of dance to and a bit of wine, but not something that costs so much money.

I do think that we go overboard with this type of thing, but it is your own personal taste and of course it's supposed to be a once-in-a-lifetime thing that we do, so I guess that's why people do spend so much money. What about you? What's your ideal wedding?

lessons.title: What athlete do you admire?
lessons.description: One Minute English video lesson for High-Intermediate learners.
lessons.transcriptHtml:
Hide / Show Transcript

Hello, everyone. My name is Gian, and I'm from Brazil. My question right now is, what athlete do I admire?

I am not a big sports person. I had my periods in life that I was either watching soccer or now that I live in the United States, definitely watching more basketball. So definitely there were people that I was just like, "Wow, these people are very talented." In soccer, Ronaldinho Gaúcho. In basketball, my latest athlete was definitely Stephen Curry. I had the privilege to see Usain Bolt running as well. That guy is just incredible. Probably for the ones that are alive right now, I would say Usain Bolt. But if I have to choose one, it's definitely going to be Bruce Lee.

I said I'm not big into sports, but the only sport that I do and have practiced since I was very young is martial arts, and kung fu, and kickboxing. So I'm definitely into the martial arts aspect of it. Not the big fighting, UFC, super violent thing, but the more artistic, but impactful arts or martial arts. And Bruce Lee would definitely be one of my biggest admirations. Not only by his amazing technique and power but also the philosophy on life and all the wisdom he carries. So I guess he'd be my choice for the athlete that I admire the most. Alright, guys, hope to see you soon.

lessons.description: One Minute English video lesson for High-Intermediate learners.
lessons.transcriptHtml:
Hide / Show Transcript

What do I usually eat for breakfast? Actually, everybody here in my country Algeria, eats French breakfast, which is milk and coffee with croissant. And I do, too.

The reason is because we were once occupied by the French colonialism, and their colonialism wasn't military. It was cultural. They came here, they tried to give us their habits, their religion, their language. They changed many things about us, about our habits, for example the breakfast, or for example the language. I actually speak French just as good as Arabic. But before the colonialism, we used to have Turkish or Syrian breakfast, which is cheese and juice and tea and olive and eggs. The healthy breakfast.

Hello everyone. My name is Gian, and I'm from Brazil. My question right now is, if I like to wear jewelry.

Well, probably not. I do wear my wedding ring. That is very special to me. My wedding ring, it was actually given from my grandparents to my parents, and now me and my wife, my wife and I, use them. So, they are over 70 years old, seven-zero. So, it's a long time, and have their names here. That's probably my only jewelry that I use often.

I'm very mystical and spiritual person. So, every so often, you see me wear a crystal, or a bracelet with different stones, but yeah, not very big into wearing anything. I'm all about being comfortable. This is my workspace, so I'm always wearing really comfy clothes. The older I get, I'm less and less worried about how do I look to people. So, I'm always using sweatpants and all of that. So, I think I would say probably, no, I do not like to wear jewelry. All right, guys. I hope to see you next time. Bye-bye.

Hide / Show Transcript

Hi. My name is Nev and I'm from Canada. And my question for today is, is your family international? Do they travel a lot?

Hi. My name is Bo. And I'm from the Philippines. And I'll be answering the question, what is a city you visited not long ago?

The last city I visited was Shanghai in China. I've been to Shanghai twice already, and it always fascinates me. The city is very advanced when you talk about their infrastructure and their transportation system. Plus it's very tourist-friendly. You can also go to Shanghai Disneyland if you are into theme parks. One of the things I look forward to when I go to Shanghai is the maglev train ride from the airport to the city. Maglev stands for magnetic levitation. So the train is floating and it travels at a speed of 300 kilometers per hour or more, which would only take you about five minutes to get to the city. If you ever need a destination for your next trip, put Shanghai on the list.

lessons.title: Do you follow astrology?
lessons.description: One Minute English video lesson for High-Intermediate learners.
lessons.transcriptHtml:
Hide / Show Transcript

Hello, my name's Elaine. I'm from England. My question today do you follow astrology?

I read my horoscopes, not every day, maybe once or twice a week. Sometimes, I forget to read them completely, so they're not really that important to me, but I do read them. I read them usually when I'm a little bit uncertain about what to do with my life, or I have a decision to make. I'll find myself lingering over the horoscopes a little bit longer than normal. I know which star sign I am. I know which star sign my mum is, any potential friends are.

I feel like we can gain a little bit of insight into people's characters based on their star sign. Although, I don't take it too seriously. I think some people use horoscopes and astrology in the same way that they use religion. They need guidance and a connection to the universe, a bigger picture to understand where they're going in their lives, that give them some direction, just in the same way that other people use religion. So, it's different for everybody. What about you? Do you believe in astrology, or do you believe in something different?

lessons.title: Where did you go for your last vacation?
lessons.description: One Minute English video lesson for High-Intermediate learners.
lessons.transcriptHtml:
Hi, I'm Olivia. I'm from Washington DC and my question is, where did you go for your last vacation?

It was in what must have been May. We went to Spain. So I used to live right outside of Barcelona in a town called Sits, which is right on the coast. It's a beautiful little vacation town. So I lived there for three years and I wanted to go back and visit and, oh, hello cat, and show my boyfriend where I lived. So that was beautiful. We stayed there for about three days. Enjoyed the beach. It was sunny, but not too warm. And then we went to Madrid to visit my other two friends that I met while I was living in Spain, and spent about two and a half days with them, and it made my heart so happy to see them again. And then we went to Saville. I haven't been to Saville ever, and that was really exciting and that was fun because that was the part of the trip that I didn't plan. I left it up to him, so everything we did was kind of a surprise, and we spent about two days there. So yeah, my last holiday in Spain, I loved it very much and I am desperate to go back. So hopefully within the next couple of months I can book in a trip to go back, even if it's just a short one.

Meaning: Located directly next to the ocean or sea.

Examples:

Examples:

  2. This soup is tasty but not too spicy.

Examples:

  2. Hearing her laugh made my heart so happy.

Meaning: Let someone else decide or take control.

Examples:

  1. I left it up to him to plan the trip.
  2. She left it up to her kids to choose the movie.

desperate to

Examples:

  1. I am desperate to go back.
  2. He was desperate to find his lost phone.

Examples:

  2. Hopefully it won’t rain tomorrow.

  2. I plan to finish the project within the next couple of days.

Examples:

lessons.title: Do you prefer shopping at a mall or online?
lessons.description: One Minute English video lesson for High-Intermediate learners.
lessons.transcriptHtml:
Hi, I'm Stacy. I am Australian and I live in Edinburgh. And my question is, if I prefer shopping in a shopping mall or online.

A hundred percent prefer shopping online. I will often have several shopping baskets open with things in it at a time just because I just love having a little wishlist of things I want to buy. I love the beauty that you can shop anytime, anywhere in your pajamas with a cup of tea, with your favorite TV show in the background. And I just love seeing what's out there. I have specific shops that I buy from most of the time, so I know what size I am, so I don't need to go in and try things on. I know that I'm a size whatever in this top, and I'll be a size or whatever in those jeans, and it's just simple and it's easy and it comes to you in a few days. You don't have to leave your house. I think it's great, and I love it, and I'm just so glad it's now a thing that we can do every day because it's just so easy.

lessons.title: Have you ever been lost?
lessons.description: One Minute English video lesson for High-Intermediate learners.
lessons.transcriptHtml:
Hide / Show Transcript

Hello, my name is Bianca and I'm from North Carolina in the United States. My question is have you ever been lost?

Have I ever been lost? Yes. I've been lost countless times even with the GPS, but thankfully today I am better than I used to be because in the past, I would get on the metro going in the wrong direction, or I would walk in circles and end up late to an appointment that I was supposed to be at.

Nowadays, because I know that I'm a person with a compromised sense of direction, I like to prepare beforehand. So that means looking up the directions to a place and also giving myself a buffer of time just in case I do get lost. Oftentimes for a very important event, I'll do a dry run of the route the day before. So I will look up the directions and I will take them the day before to make sure I know what I'm doing and where I'm going the day of and I don't arrive late.

Again, generally I'm much better than I used to be. In the United States, being late is sort of frowned upon, so I try to do everything I can to arrive on time or early. And it's also less stressful for me. If all else fails, then I will request an Uber or a Lyft. And I like to give buffer time for the driver just in case he or she gets lost as well. But again, generally I am much better than I used to be. And that is thanks to technology. So thank you so much. And what about you? Have you ever been lost.

  • Review the vocabulary from the video below.
  • Complete the blanks below with words from the lesson.
  • Check your answers. Correct any answers that are wrong!

countless times

Meaning: Very many times; too many to count.

Examples:

  1. I have watched that movie countless times.
  2. She has visited Paris countless times.

in circles

Meaning: Moving without making progress; going around the same place.

Examples:

  1. We drove in circles looking for the restaurant.
  2. I keep going in circles with this problem at work.

end up late

Meaning: To arrive somewhere later than planned.

Examples:

  1. We ended up late because of traffic.
  2. If you don’t hurry, you’ll end up late for the meeting.

compromised sense of direction

Meaning: Having poor ability to know which way to go.

Examples:

  1. He has a compromised sense of direction and often gets lost.
  2. Because of my compromised sense of direction, I always carry a map.

looking up

Meaning: Searching for information (usually online or in a book).

Examples:

  1. I am looking up the train schedule.
  2. She looked up the word in the dictionary.

buffer

Meaning: Extra time or space to prevent problems.

Examples:

  1. I left early to give myself a buffer in case of traffic.
  2. Always add a buffer to your budget for unexpected costs.

just in case

Meaning: To be prepared for something that might happen.

Examples:

  1. Bring an umbrella just in case it rains.
  2. I saved her number just in case I need help.

oftentimes

Meaning: Frequently; many times.

Examples:

  1. Oftentimes, I work from home.
  2. She oftentimes visits her parents on weekends.

dry run

Meaning: Practice or test before the real event.

Examples:

  1. We did a dry run of the presentation before the meeting.
  2. The team had a dry run before the opening ceremony.

frowned upon

Meaning: Not approved of; looked at as bad.

Examples:

  1. Cheating is frowned upon in our school.
  2. Smoking indoors is frowned upon in many countries.

if all else fails

Meaning: If nothing else works.

Examples:

  1. If all else fails, I’ll call a taxi.
  2. If all else fails, we can try again tomorrow.

lessons.title: What product is in high demand?
lessons.description: One Minute English video lesson for High-Intermediate learners.
lessons.transcriptHtml:
Hi, my name is Billy, and I will be talking today about what product is on high demand.

So this is a very interesting topic because I think products depends on who you're asking and also the gender. Like for example, for females, I think the highest product on demand right now is makeup or cosmetic materials. And you have so many brands. You have your Kylie Jenner brands, you have Fenty, I think by Rihanna. There's so many products that are on high demand, but I think the cosmetic industry is booming right now. So those products are going to be on higher demand. I think if you ask guys, the highest demand would probably be maybe a car or some, like yeah, a car with a V8 engine or something like that. Maybe a watch.

So I think it depends on the gender and also the age gap in which you're going for. But a product that I think will always be on high demand is food. Right now, I think we need more food than ever before, and it's the highest demand that we can get. So yeah, let's keep that product on lower demand, make sure everybody has food to eat and such.

So yeah, that's my take.

lessons.description: One Minute English video lesson for High-Intermediate learners.
lessons.transcriptHtml:
My name is Ahmed. I come from Egypt, and my question is, who is a famous person that you would like to meet?

Now, this is very obvious to me, and it's a psychologist called Dr. Jordan Peterson. This professor of psychology has really helped me become the person that I am today. So I credit a lot of who I am as a person to his knowledge and to his being, whatever that means. Honestly, he affected my life in a very, very good way. He had a lot of insights that I was not aware of. He helped me push myself. He helped me become a better person for myself, for my spouse, for my family, for everyone around me, for society. I think he is a wonderful person as far as I know him to be, at least from what he communicates, from how he seems to be online, which I think is true.

So yeah, I would definitely, if I could meet anyone right now, it would definitely be him just to show him some appreciation for his work and how it affected my life.

lessons.title: What social media apps have you stopped using and why?
lessons.description: One Minute English video lesson for High-Intermediate learners.
lessons.transcriptHtml:
My name is Ahmed. I come from Egypt. And my question is, what social media apps have you stopped using and why?

So I have stopped using Instagram because it wastes a lot of my time. I already have YouTube for mindless scrolling, so I did not think I needed another source of distraction in my life. Especially with Instagram, it's very easy to get lost scrolling on your phone, and so I made the decision to completely get rid of it, which annoyed my girlfriend a bit because she likes to send me memes. But yeah, I stopped using Instagram and I, Hey, I would encourage you to do so as well, and I would really encourage you to reconsider your position on how much time you're spending on social media apps in general.

lessons.title: What is your favorite food?
lessons.description: One Minute English video lesson for High-Intermediate learners.
lessons.transcriptHtml:
Hi, I'm Stacy. I'm Australian, and I live in Scotland, and my question is, what is my favorite food?

Well, I have two sushi and chocolate, but not together. I love sushi. I love this restaurant that I go to in Edinburgh and it has the most amazing sushi. I like to get the rainbow roll, which is tuna and salmon and cucumber and avocado, but it's also the way that it's beautifully presented. There is such an artistry to making sushi, and I just appreciate everything that goes into it, and I savor every bite. I just want to eat more and more and more. I could sit there for hours and just eating little bits here and there. I just love it. Chocolate, I mean, who doesn't love chocolate? It's sweet. It's comfort food. It's lovely when you dip it into your tea or your coffee and it melts a little bit. I love chocolate on strawberries. If you haven't tried that, give it a try. It's delicious. I just love chocolate and I love sushi, and that's me, and that makes me so happy.

lessons.title: Would you ever get plastic surgery?
lessons.description: One Minute English video lesson for High-Intermediate learners.
lessons.transcriptHtml:
Hide / Show Transcript

Hi, I'm Bo, and I'm from the Philippines. And I will be answering the question would you ever get plastic surgery?

I am open to the possibility of getting plastic surgery. If something makes you happy and confident, even if it involves enhancing something physically with the help of plastic surgery, then by all means, go for it. It is also inappropriate to go out there and judge people who have done it, because we don't know the actual reason of them having the surgery. They might have undergone surgery due to an existing problem with their face or skin, while some do it for enhancement. Whatever the reason is, everyone deserves respect, and it never hurts to respect other people.

lessons.title: Is life better or worse in this digital era?
lessons.description: One Minute English video lesson for High-Intermediate learners.
lessons.transcriptHtml:
Hi, my name is Billy and I am currently living in South Africa. My question today is life better or worse in this digital era?

Okay, so one thing is we sure life is better because you're able to watch this video and I'm able to make this video for you to watch. So I would say life is great with that. However, I would say that it actually depends because although life is supposedly increasing with the amount of technology that we are exposed to right now, I think the quality of life has decreased. There's a lot of people that are digitally connected or digitally informed.

However, quality wise, the quality of their friendship, the quality of their connections, or even just the quality of the entertainment that they are exposed to or their watch has decreased to a severe level. Although life is better because I can call you at any time and you can answer. I think that it's very hard for people to keep a quality of life that makes them happy and that makes them feel fulfilled.

What about you? Do you think life is better or worse in this digital era? I'd like to hear from you.

lessons.title: Do you like working out in gyms?
lessons.description: One Minute English video lesson for High-Intermediate learners.
lessons.transcriptHtml:
Hi, I'm Stacy. I am Australian, and I live in Scotland. And my question is, do I like working out in gyms?

And the answer is a big, fat no. I hate it. I have had probably three or four gym memberships in the last 20 years, and I've not really used any of them. I canceled them because I was just wasting my money.

It's very hard to feel motivated to go to the gym when you actually do get there. I just find it really boring. I don't like working out on equipment that other people have sweated on, and I don't like doing those kinds of exercise classes. I find them kind of boring.

I'm a dancer, so to me, dancing is my exercise, and I love it. So it's exercise in disguise. I work up a sweat, I get my heart pumping, and I much prefer that than a gym membership.

It's just, it's not for me. I think for some people they love it and it works, especially if you work somewhere very close to the gym or you get your gym workout done before work, and then you've done it for the day and it's out of the way.

But it's just not my cup of tea, not for me.

lessons.title: Would you ever get plastic surgery?
lessons.description: One Minute English video lesson for High-Intermediate learners.
lessons.transcriptHtml:
Will I ever get plastic surgery?

No. I think I will never get plastic surgery. It's because I'm secure about myself and the way I look, and I think I'm beautiful the way I am, even though I'm not perfect.

And I believe that this is what everybody else should be doing, loving themselves the way they are, because nobody's ugly. Everybody's beautiful. Trust me. If you are clean and organized, you are beautiful, and you do not need to change anything about yourself, especially your look.

So if the plastic surgery is done due to medical reasons or after an accident, I'm totally fine with it. I support it.

But if somebody's changing their facial features or something in their body in order to please somebody else, no, I'm totally against this, and I would never do it because I love myself, and I never want to hurt myself to please other people.
