lessons.transcriptHtml:
Hello, my name is Cruz. I'm from Argentina. My question is, what is your favorite idiom, proverb, or saying?

Well, my favorite saying is “nothing ventured, nothing gained,” which means if you don't take any chances or risks, you won't gain anything. So whenever you want to get something in your life, you will have to take action.

No matter what people say, no matter your fears, no matter rejection, no matter things getting a little hard, there's no way things will happen just by staying home, lying in your bed.

So, you have to take things which are risky or which might be hard for you, or you might lose something, but it is the only way you can get to your goals.

How to Practice Vocabulary

  • Review the vocabulary.
  • Complete the blanks below with correct words.
  • Check your answers. Correct any wrong answers!

idiom

Meaning: A group of words with a meaning different from the individual words.

Examples:

  1. “Break the ice” is a common idiom.
  2. “Spill the beans” is an idiom meaning to reveal a secret.

proverb

Meaning: A short, wise saying that gives advice.

Examples:

  1. “Actions speak louder than words” is a proverb.
  2. My grandmother always used proverbs to give advice.

saying

Meaning: A common expression or phrase that shares a truth or idea.

Examples:

  1. “Better late than never” is a popular saying.
  2. That saying really makes you think.

ventured

Meaning: Took a risk or tried something risky.

Examples:

  1. He ventured into starting his own business.
  2. She ventured to speak in front of a big crowd.

gained

Meaning: Got or achieved something.

Examples:

  1. He gained confidence by practicing every day.
  2. She gained experience from her part-time job.

take action

Meaning: To do something to make a change.

Examples:

  1. You must take action if you want results.
  2. It’s time to stop thinking and take action.

no matter

Meaning: Regardless of; not affected by something.

Examples:

  1. Keep going, no matter what others say.
  2. I’ll support you, no matter the result.

rejection

Meaning: Being refused or not accepted.

Examples:

  1. Rejection is part of trying new things.
  2. Don’t fear rejection—just try again.

lessons.title: Are you a tenant or home owner?
lessons.description: One Minute English video lesson for High-Intermediate learners.
lessons.transcriptHtml:
Hi, my name is Billy, and I am currently living in South Africa. And my question today is, am I a house owner or am I a tenant?

So, simple answer, I am a tenant. I think it's a lot of work to be a house owner, and also it's very expensive. I would need a little bit more saving to be able to get there.

I don't know. In South Africa, property is kind of expensive, but you can get decent properties, but it needs a bit more planning and a little bit more of the money aspect and credits and everything.

So I'm very happy to be a tenant because there's also less responsibility on my side if anything's broken or whatever. I can ask my house owner or my landlord to fix it, especially if it was there when I arrived.

Okay, so that's me. What about you? Would you like to be a house owner? Or maybe you are a house owner. Are you enjoying it? Or if you're not a house owner, are you enjoying being a tenant? Let me know. Bye.

  • Review the vocabulary.
  • Complete the blanks below with correct words.
  • Check your answers. Correct any wrong answers!

tenant

Meaning: A person who rents a place to live.

Examples:

  1. I’m a tenant in an apartment downtown.
  2. The tenant pays rent to the landlord.

decent

Meaning: Good enough; acceptable in quality.

Examples:

  1. You can find decent housing in that area.
  2. The room was small but decent and clean.

properties

Meaning: Houses or buildings that people own.

Examples:

  1. They bought two properties last year.
  2. That company sells luxury properties.

aspect

Meaning: One part or side of something.

Examples:

  1. The financial aspect of buying a house is hard.
  2. Every aspect of the plan was discussed.

credit

Meaning: Money borrowed, usually from a bank, to pay later.

Examples:

  1. Buying a house often involves taking out credit.
  2. He used credit to finance the home.

that's me

Meaning: That describes who I am or my situation.

Examples:

  1. I like simple living—that’s me.
  2. I prefer renting. That’s me for now.

on my side

Meaning: My responsibility or part of the situation.

Examples:

  1. If something breaks, it's not on my side to fix it.
  2. There’s less pressure on my side as a tenant.

lessons.title: What do you think about long distance relationships?
lessons.description: One Minute English video lesson for High-Intermediate learners.
lessons.transcriptHtml:
My name is Ahmed. I come from Egypt. And my question is, what do you think about long-distance relationships?

I have been in a long distance relationship for a little bit more than two years. I would say don't do it. Don't do it. Don't do it at all. Unless you have very strong evidence to believe that the person you are with is too valuable for you to let them go, or some variation of them being too important in your life for you not to fight against life itself, oftentimes against them. Against yourself to make them… to do your best, to influence them to stay in your life, let's say.

So in general, I think it's a very difficult enterprise to manage on both parties. I think a lot of times, typical problems in a relationship get magnified because of the distance. So there are a lot of problems with a long-distance relationship, absolutely. Is it doable? I think so. I hope so. So I would say be cautious and be responsible.

How to Practice Vocabulary

  • Review the vocabulary.
  • Complete the blanks below with correct words.
  • Check your answers. Correct any wrong answers!

long-distance relationship

Meaning: A romantic relationship where two people live far apart and cannot see each other often.

Examples:

  1. Maintaining a long distance relationship requires strong communication and trust.
  2. They have been in a long distance relationship for three years, but they make it work.

strong evidence

Meaning: Clear proof or convincing reasons to believe something.

Examples:

  1. There is strong evidence that exercising regularly improves health.
  2. Before making a decision, you should have strong evidence that it’s the right choice.

let them go

Meaning: To allow someone to leave your life, emotionally or physically.

Examples:

  1. If someone doesn’t treat you well, it’s best to let them go.
  2. She didn’t want to let him go, but she knew it was the right decision.

some variation of

Meaning: A different form or version of something.

Examples:

  1. Most love stories are some variation of "boy meets girl, they fall in love, and something happens."
  2. Every culture has some variation of traditional dance.

enterprise

Meaning: A project, challenge, or business that requires effort to manage.

Examples:

  1. Running a small business is a difficult enterprise that requires patience.
  2. A long distance relationship is a challenging enterprise that requires dedication from both people.

let’s say

Meaning: A phrase used to introduce an example or possibility.

Examples:

  1. Let’s say you move to another country—how would you keep in touch?
  2. If you could live anywhere, let’s say Paris, would you do it?

both parties

Meaning: Both people or groups involved in something.

Examples:

  1. Both parties need to communicate well for a relationship to work.
  2. In business deals, both parties must agree on the contract terms.

lessons.title: Do you prefer natural or modern medicine?
lessons.description: One Minute English video lesson for High-Intermediate learners.
lessons.transcriptHtml:
The question that I'm answering today is, do I prefer natural or modern medicine?

Now, in my experience in my family, we have utilized both. The natural component is in the form of traditional Chinese medicines, where you boil roots and herbs to treat ailments. And of course, the modern medicine is the medicine in the hospital as we know of it today.

Now for me, I prefer modern medicine more because personally I have trained in the area as a health professional. So I understand the science, I've seen the process, and I also like how each of the treatments provided do have a form of research and proof associated with it.

Now, that's not to say that the natural ways are not correct because so much of the modern medicine is based also on what we've found in natural medicines as well, but more refined to match a certain condition. So personally, I have used both, but I prefer modern medicine.
lessons.vocabularyHtml:
How to Practice Vocabulary

  • Review the vocabulary.
  • Complete the blanks below with correct words.
  • Check your answers. Correct any wrong answers!

natural component

Meaning: A part of something that comes from nature, such as herbs or plants used in medicine.

Examples:

  1. Many traditional remedies include a natural component like herbs or roots.
  2. The natural component of this treatment comes from medicinal plants.

treat ailments

Meaning: To use medicine or remedies to cure or relieve sickness or health problems.

Examples:

  1. Herbal tea is often used to treat ailments like sore throats and colds.
  2. Modern medicine provides effective ways to treat ailments such as infections.

trained in the area

Meaning: Having professional education or experience in a specific field.

Examples:

  1. She is trained in the area of nutrition and gives advice on healthy eating.
  2. As a doctor, he is trained in the area of emergency medicine.

proof

Meaning: Evidence that shows something is true or correct.

Examples:

  1. Scientific research provides proof that vaccines are effective.
  2. We need proof before believing any health claims.

associated with

Meaning: Connected or related to something.

Examples:

  1. Smoking is associated with many health problems.
  2. Regular exercise is associated with a lower risk of heart disease.

that's not to say

Meaning: A phrase used to clarify that you are not completely rejecting something.

Examples:

  1. I love coffee, but that's not to say I never drink tea.
  2. She prefers modern medicine, but that's not to say natural remedies don’t work.

refined

Meaning: Improved or made more effective through changes and improvements.

Examples:

  1. Modern medicine is refined to ensure safety and effectiveness.
  2. The recipe has been refined over the years to make it taste better.

certain condition

Meaning: A specific illness or health issue that requires treatment.

Examples:

  1. This drug is used to treat a certain condition related to heart disease.
  2. Different herbs can help with certain conditions, but not all illnesses.

lessons.title: What was it like growing up on a farm?
lessons.description: One Minute English video lesson for High-Intermediate learners.
lessons.transcriptHtml:
Hi, I am Olivia. I'm from Washington DC and my question is, what was it like growing up on a farm?

Well, I did not grow up on a farm, but my dad did and my cousins do, and their lives are very different from me, but I can tell you what I've heard from what I can tell. Growing up on a farm, you are far more physically competent, and you have a much more stricter schedule in terms of chores because often you have to help out, and you have a lot of freedom going outside, within the countryside, because at least my dad and my cousins, they lived on a farm with lots of space, so they could kind of go out and explore all day, and their parents wouldn't really ask where they've gone. They knew they were somewhere on the land, but when it comes to being around in a city, they're not as comfortable maneuvering around that way.

My cousins had lots of horses and animals and pigs, and they were always kind of feeding them, and they were just much more physically competent. They knew if one of them was hurt, how to fix them. They knew their schedule. They were far more resilient, whereas I was a bit more squeamish with those things whenever I visited. Yeah, my dad used to have to get up at 5:00 AM to help on the farm before school. He was very, very diligent in getting all of his tasks done, but then when he moved to Big City, he was a bit more like... So, yeah, I think it's a very free lifestyle in some ways and also strict in other ways, but in a completely different way than it is from growing up in the city.

How to Practice Vocabulary

  • Review the vocabulary.
  • Complete the blanks below with correct words.
  • Check your answers. Correct any wrong answers!

physically competent

Meaning: Having good physical skills and the ability to handle physical tasks well.

Examples:

  1. People who grow up on farms tend to be more physically competent because they do a lot of manual work.
  2. She is very physically competent, so she excels at sports and outdoor activities.

whereas

Meaning: Used to contrast two different things.

Examples:

  1. He enjoys outdoor activities, whereas I prefer staying indoors.
  2. My cousins grew up on a farm, whereas I grew up in a big city.

maneuvering around

Meaning: Moving or finding one's way through a place or situation.

Examples:

  1. He had trouble maneuvering around the crowded streets of New York.
  2. Farmers are comfortable working in open fields, but they may struggle maneuvering around in big cities.

resilient

Meaning: Able to recover quickly from difficulties; strong and adaptable.

Examples:

  1. People who work on farms are often very resilient because they deal with tough conditions.
  2. She faced many challenges, but she remained resilient and never gave up.

squeamish

Meaning: Easily uncomfortable or scared, especially about blood, injuries, or unpleasant things.

Examples:

  1. I feel squeamish when I see blood.
  2. He is squeamish about touching insects, but his cousin loves playing with them.

diligent

Meaning: Hardworking and careful in completing tasks.

Examples:

  1. She is very diligent in her studies and always submits her homework on time.
  2. Farmers have to be diligent to make sure all their animals are fed properly.

in some ways, in other ways

Meaning: Used to compare different aspects of something.

Examples:

  1. In some ways, living on a farm is fun, but in other ways, it is very hard work.
  2. In some ways, moving to a city was exciting, but in other ways, it was overwhelming.

lessons.title: What is the key to happiness?
lessons.description: One Minute English video lesson for High-Intermediate learners.
lessons.transcriptHtml:
My name is Ahmed. I come from Egypt, and my question is, what is the key to happiness?

Which I think is a difficult question to answer, but despite me being an ignorant 24-year-old, I will do my best to answer it.

I think first of all, we should, instead of making all this effort to be happy, which happens to be what society generally is talking about nowadays, I think we should focus on being thankful for what we have.

I think if you have people in your life that you care about and then they care about you and they're healthy when you wake up every morning, I think that's something that you should absolutely not take for granted. You should be very, very thankful for that.

So I would say try to be more thankful in general. For something a bit more practical, I would say oftentimes when I'm concerned about something, some event, it's because there's something that has an outcome that I can't control in the future, and I want a specific outcome to be the outcome that actually happens.

And what I would say is we should try to do our best. Look at what we can do to influence the outcome, do our best to influence it, and that should be our goal. I think that is the key to happiness.
lessons.vocabularyHtml:
How to Practice Vocabulary

  • Review the vocabulary.
  • Complete the blanks below with correct words.
  • Check your answers. Correct any wrong answers!

ignorant

Meaning: Lacking knowledge or understanding about something.

Examples:

  1. I was ignorant about cooking until I took a class.
  2. He admitted that he was ignorant about the topic but wanted to learn.

making all this effort

Meaning: Trying very hard to do something.

Examples:

  1. She is making all this effort to learn French before her trip.
  2. We are making all this effort to improve the project, but no one appreciates it.

focus on

Meaning: To give attention to something.

Examples:

  1. Instead of worrying, focus on what you can control.
  2. She tries to focus on her studies instead of social media.

take for granted

Meaning: To not appreciate something because it is always there.

Examples:

  1. Many people take for granted the love and support of their families.
  2. We often take for granted having clean water and electricity.

practical

Meaning: Useful, realistic, or related to real-life situations.

Examples:

  1. She gave me practical advice on how to save money.
  2. Learning how to cook is a practical skill everyone should have.

outcome

Meaning: The result of something happening.

Examples:

  1. The outcome of the test will decide if I pass the course.
  2. We can’t control the outcome, but we can do our best.

in general

Meaning: Usually; considering everything.

Examples:

  1. In general, I try to eat healthy food.
  2. In general, life is easier when you stay positive.

lessons.title: Do you have a special pet?
lessons.description: One Minute English video lesson for High-Intermediate learners.
lessons.transcriptHtml:
The question I'm answering is, do I have a special pet?

And yes, I do have a special pet, and his name is Cooper. So, Cooper is a dog that we have, and he's of the breed King Charles Cavalier. The King Charles Cavalier were bred to be companion dogs, and they have a mild temperament and are good with children, but our dog that's quite special is nothing like that.

He runs around, he pulls; he's a bit aggressive. He would jump all over you, but we don't mind because he's our special dog. Now he has white and brown fur, and this mix is usually called a Blenheim color, and he loves to eat everything. He chews different parts of the house. He'll eat your socks. But we still love him because he is our special pet.
lessons.vocabularyHtml:
How to Practice Vocabulary

  • Review the vocabulary.
  • Complete the blanks below with correct words.
  • Check your answers. Correct any wrong answers!

breed

Meaning: A specific type or group of animals with similar characteristics, especially dogs.

Examples:

  1. The Labrador Retriever is a popular dog breed.
  2. My cat is of the Siamese breed and has blue eyes.

companion dogs

Meaning: Dogs that are bred to provide company and emotional support rather than work or hunting.

Examples:

  1. Poodles and Pomeranians are common companion dogs.
  2. Companion dogs are great for people who live alone.

we don't mind

Meaning: We are okay with something; it doesn’t bother us.

Examples:

  1. The kids make a mess, but we don’t mind because they are having fun.
  2. Our dog barks a lot, but we don’t mind because he protects the house.

aggressive

Meaning: Showing strong, sometimes violent behavior.

Examples:

  1. Some dogs are naturally aggressive, while others are calm.
  2. He became aggressive when he lost the game.

runs around

Meaning: Moves quickly from place to place.

Examples:

  1. The children run around the playground after school.
  2. My dog runs around the house whenever he gets excited.

jump all over you

Meaning: To jump on someone repeatedly, often in excitement.

Examples:

  1. My dog will jump all over you when you enter the house.
  2. The kids jumped all over me when they saw I had brought gifts.

fur

Meaning: The thick hair that covers the bodies of some animals, like dogs or cats.

Examples:

  1. My cat has soft gray fur.
  2. The dog’s white fur gets dirty easily.

Blenheim

Meaning: A color pattern of white and brown, commonly found in Cavalier King Charles Spaniels.

Examples:

  1. Our dog has the Blenheim coloring—brown and white patches.
  2. Many Cavalier King Charles Spaniels are Blenheim in color.

mild temperament

Meaning: A calm and gentle personality or behavior.

Examples:

  1. Golden Retrievers are known for their mild temperament.
  2. She has a mild temperament, so she rarely gets angry.

lessons.title: Where does your best friend live?
lessons.description: One Minute English video lesson for High-Intermediate learners.
lessons.transcriptHtml:
Hi, I'm Olivia. I'm from Washington DC and my question is, where does your best friend live?

My best friend lives in New York City right now. We are childhood best friends. I've known her probably since I was five, and we were best friends since we were eight, and we both loved where we grew up, but did not see ourselves living there. So I moved to London and she moved to New York City, and I really hope that one day we end up living in the same city together.

I also want to live in New York City, and she also kind of wants to live in London, and so hopefully one of us makes the choice to go somewhere and we might be able to live there together because texting and calling isn't the same as being there with the person. So she loves New York City, though that's honestly where she's thriving and she's doing really well. She's got a great job, so I'm really proud of her, but I do miss her and I do wish that we were in the same location.

lessons.title: What was your first job?
lessons.description: One Minute English video lesson for High-Intermediate learners.
lessons.transcriptHtml:
Hi, I'm Stacy. I am Australian and I live in Scotland. And my question is, what is my first job?

My first job was actually working in McDonald's. I was 18. I had just finished school. It's actually really good first job, especially in Australia. I find if you've got McDonald's as your first job in your CV as a reference, it really holds up.

It was good fun. Most of the people that work there are sort of age between, I would say 15 to 25, so really sociable and yeah, you get really good experience and you can work with people and customers, and you do come home smelling like french fries. You've got to come home and have a shower. You also tend to get a bit of an oily skin from being around the frying machine, but I also learned to work at the back in the kitchen, which is also really good fun and just a change of pace from serving customers.

But yeah, I did it for a year and a half while I was at university, and it was a really good first job.

lessons.title: How do you feel about superhero movies?
lessons.description: One Minute English video lesson for Advanced learners.
lessons.transcriptHtml:
Hello, I'm Victoria. I'm from Suriname. And my question is, what or how do you feel about superhero movies? Love them or hate them?

I love superhero movies because I find them inspiring. We all know, or at least I hope we all know, that superhero movies are fantasy, but still it provides us with a number of things. The first one is an escape from reality for at least an hour. The second thing that I get from a superhero movie is that anything is possible. Of course, in a movie, it's exaggerated, fantasized. But one thing that I can take away from a superhero movie is that we can do things which we otherwise wouldn't think would be possible. And to be honest, don't we all dream about having superpowers. So watching such a movie, identifying with a character in such a movie, is invigorating, I believe. So I love superhero movies.

lessons.title: Which work location do you prefer your current to previous job?
lessons.description: One Minute English video lesson for Advanced learners.
lessons.transcriptHtml:
Hello, my name is Tarren and I am from the United States of America. My question is the following: which work location do you prefer, your current to previous job?

I prefer my current job, hands down. I am a full-time on camera and voiceover actress, and I'm extremely grateful to be able to do what I love every single day. It's something that I've worked towards for a very long time. I was previously a personal trainer, nutritionist, and yoga teacher, and I still hold those certifications and I will continue to hold those certifications. So I am technically still a master level fitness professional, but I no longer work for companies in the industry at this point in time on an employment basis. I do independent contracting by promoting companies or being a spokesperson, but I don't have any clients that I'm working with currently training or giving nutritional advice to or things like that.

And that's just because I didn't have the best experience in the fitness industry as a woman and as a business professional, and I'm extremely grateful to do what I love every day as an actress now, as a fully self-employed business owner.

lessons.title: Should people take law into their own hands?
lessons.description: One Minute English video lesson for Advanced learners.
lessons.transcriptHtml:
Hi, my name is Billie and I am currently living in South Africa. And my question today is, should people take law into their own hands?

Simple answer, no. The reason I say this is because we come from such different backgrounds culturally, and also just family life and certain morals and upbringing is a whole lot different from one culture to another, even in the same country. So, I think if everyone was just to decide as to what law would fit best a circumstance, it would make the world a lot more chaotic because what I feel is just and fair, somebody from a different culture or somebody even just next door to me might feel that that was not fair and it could have been handled differently. So, I think the law is there to make sure that everyone does get treated equally, although sometimes that equality slips through the cracks, but I think that they are trying their best.

Anyways, that's just my opinion. What about you? What do you think? Should people take the law into their own hands? Let me know.

lessons.title: What worries you more, the environment or the economy?
lessons.description: One Minute English video lesson for Advanced learners.
lessons.transcriptHtml:
Hi, my name is Saif and I'm from Pakistan. And my question is, what worries me more, the environment or the economy?

I worry about the environment more than the economy. My country is an agriculture country and its economy is greatly reliant on agriculture and livestock produce. An unhealthy environment is bad for product, which will lead to poor business and as a result hurt the economy. The economy is thus greatly dependent on the environment, which makes me worried since excessive industrialization, increased infrastructure, deforestation and deoceanization is harming the environment exponentially through inefficient toxic waste disposal, air and sea pollution, leading to deteriorating ozone layer and poor environment.

lessons.title: What would you change about the educational system in your country?
lessons.description: One Minute English video lesson for Advanced learners.
lessons.transcriptHtml:
Hi, my name is Alexis and I'm from the United States. And my question today is what would you change about the educational system in your country?

So, I am in school to be a teacher. I will be a certified teacher in the next three months. And I've had a lot of experiences in schools, and I do think that overall it is okay. But I do think one of the main things that I would focus on is really ensuring that no kid gets left behind or falls through the cracks because I do feel like education, it's getting better, but it is very general and a lot of what is taught isn't to fit the needs of all students. So that's probably what I would change the most, but I only have about a minute to answer this question and I could go on for an hour.

lessons.title: What is a hardship that you've dealt with in the past?
lessons.description: One Minute English video lesson for Advanced learners.
lessons.transcriptHtml:
Hello, my name is Rocio, and I am from El Salvador. My question is, what is a hardship that you've dealt with in the past?

I feel like my most memorable hardship for me or the most game changing one for me was when I got my first job out of high school. I was 18 and I had applied for this interpretation job. And since I already knew how to speak English, I thought that it was going to be really easy, but later on I discovered that it was going to be a medical interpretation job, and I got really, really scared, really intimidated by my coworkers and by the responsibilities that I was going to have. It was really scary at the beginning and the way that I dealt with it was really by studying really hard and putting myself into a mindset of failing. I feel like once I got myself into a mindset that, yeah, "I'm going to fail, but I'm going to learn" sort of way of thinking. I feel like that made me thrive even more in the job. And at the end of the day, I was able to master the interpretation skills. I mean, I loved the job. I ended up being promoted actually. And looking back at it, I really appreciate that experience for me because it really allowed me to grow as a person and I feel really proud about it.

But what about you? Do you have any hardship that you've dealt with that now looking back at it is, like, pretty amazing for you?

lessons.title: How do you feel about pet cafes?
lessons.description: One Minute English video lesson for Advanced learners.
lessons.transcriptHtml:
Hello, my name is Terran and I'm from the United States of America. My question is the following: How do you feel about pet cafes?

I love the concept of a pet cafe. I think it's really cute. Especially, I think it's important to know how the animals are being treated. Like, sometimes a pet cafe means you bring your pet to the cafe, and other times it means that there are pets of the cafe within the cafe. So I think the most important thing is that the animals are being treated well, whoever owns them, right? The other thing I'll say is I would love to go to a cat cafe, but it quite literally could kill me. I'm really allergic to cats. It wouldn't kill me, but I would leave there covered in hives, having asthma, a runny nose, sneezing. And I just think I would love it if I weren't allergic to it.

But a dog cafe, oh, you best believe I would love to be a part of that.

lessons.title: Is technology making our lives better or worse?
lessons.description: One Minute English video lesson for Advanced learners.
lessons.transcriptHtml:
Hi, my name is Saif and I'm from Pakistan. And my question is, is technology making our life better or worse?

Whether you're a scientist, an army general, surgeon, engineer, or even a musician, technology not only makes our everyday life tasks easier, but also plays a vital role in strategizing, planning, and executing future plans and decisions. Now, there is a negative side to technology which we all conveniently ignore. It can be invasive to our privacy. It can hurt our interpersonal communication skills.

Extended screen time in minors has made them addicted leading to eye strain, insomnia, and in worst cases, depression. Indeed, we're building robots to replace factory workers and housemaids, but who knows, one day the same minions we train to be our slaves will be our masters.

lessons.title: If you could change your nationality, what would it be?
lessons.description: One Minute English video lesson for Advanced learners.
lessons.transcriptHtml:
Hi, my name is Saif and I'm from Pakistan. And my question is, if I could change my nationality, what would it be?

If I could change my nationality, I would change it to the nationality of the world. I don't just want to belong to a single nationality. Rather, I want the entire globe to be my nation. I want the freedom to roam around the world without a special permit, a visa, or in an invitation. I don't want to be branded a particular nation: for example, Pakistani, Indian, Japanese, African or American. I want to be known by who I am and not where I'm from. Earth is my nation. Hence, in my opinion, we should drop the notion of being nation-centric and focus on uniting as one, the human race, and thus be earth-centric.

lessons.title: If you were the leader of your country, what would you do?
lessons.description: One Minute English video lesson for Advanced learners.
lessons.transcriptHtml:
Hello. My name is Preah. I am from Belize. My question was, if you were the leader of your country, what would you do?

Wow! I'm a little taken aback by this question only because I'm very opinionated about it. If I were my country's leader, I would tell my people the truth about my abilities. Because a lot of times I think politicians, they exaggerate the things that they're able to do in order to gain votes. But there are some things that they're simply not able to do. It's not possible. It's not wise. It's not realistic.

And I would want to tell my people the truth. Tell them what are things that we can accomplish, what are things that we can do instead of filling them with useless hope of things that won't be able to come.

lessons.title: What app is very trendy these days?
lessons.description: One Minute English video lesson for Advanced learners.
lessons.transcriptHtml:
Hello, my name is Grace. I'm from South Africa, and what app is very trendy these days?

I would say an app like Duo Lingo is very trendy to the point where people can make memes about it and it's sort of well-known how the app looks depending on how many days you've missed or if you've kept up your streak of practicing languages. It's quite diverse. It's got lots of languages to learn. It allows you to learn the language itself, to practice speaking, to learn characters in some cases. And it's really useful. And I think everyone should give some sort of language app a try, but Duo Lingo seems to be the most popular to the point where they've got Duo Lingo On Ice. I know. It's quite entertaining and most of it is about learning how to sing or how to speak other languages while they sing.

And it's entertaining, but it just goes to show how widespread the app itself is.

Teacher's note:
Duo Lingo On Ice is a musical production.

lessons.title: Do you have any old items or junk you need to toss out?
lessons.description: One Minute English video lesson for Advanced learners.
lessons.transcriptHtml:
Hello, my name's Alejandro. I am from Toronto, Canada. And my question today is, do you have any old items or junk you need to toss out?

And I got to say, that question for me is easy. People are always holding onto old things that they don't need and I'm no different. Although I was raised to know that wasting is never good. So, I always try to sell things potentially or even give things that I don't need to people that need them or people that they might fit better. But we all know that that takes time and my closet is piling up. I have to donate some clothing soon, that's for sure. I have donated some of my clothing to charity shops, to thrift shops, but I'm sometimes conflicted with the places I donate to and whether or not they're charitable or if they're just looking for profit.

And if that's the case, I would rather just make the profit myself, to be honest. This has definitely become a common issue with everybody. lessons.title: Are any areas in your town run down?
lessons.description: One Minute English video lesson for Advanced learners.
lessons.transcriptHtml:
Hi, I'm Olivia. I'm originally from Washington DC, and right now I live in London. And my question is, are any areas in your town run down?

And the answer is yes, as is for every area. But particularly in London, it's a really unique place that I've never experienced anywhere else where one street can be really nice and quite affluent and have lovely cafes. And you walk 50 meters down that street and it feels completely different. It literally changes street by street and on the street. In my particular case, I live in Burmansie right near London Bridge, and it's a really nice area. Parts that are quite gentrified, so there's been a lot of money put back into that neighborhood. So lovely shops, lots of people live there. The price of living there is really, really high, but then there's still the remaining parts of the neighborhood that hasn't had that money put back into it.

And so, the corner that I live on has some really, really nice flats and apartments. And then you walk down the road and the community center building that's literally there to help people in the community as an outreach is crumbling and they've had to take it down for construction. And you kind of walk further into that street and you can just kind of feel in the area lots of buildings are falling apart. There's not been as much money put into it. The people who live there might be struggling a little bit more. So yeah, definitely, especially where I live, it changes street by street.

lessons.title: When is it okay to lie?
lessons.description: One Minute English video lesson for Advanced learners.
lessons.transcriptHtml:
Hi, my name is Saif and I'm from Pakistan. My question is, when is it okay to lie?

It's okay to lie, in my opinion, in a scenario when you are protecting someone from knowing a truth, which if they knew, they might end up reacting adversely to it and as a result harm themselves or the people around them or the environment. Most people are reactive in nature rather than rational and it would be best to hide the truth from them for the time being to keep them safe.

lessons.title: What do you do to manage stress?
lessons.description: One Minute English video lesson for Advanced learners.
lessons.transcriptHtml:
Hello. So my question was, what do you do to manage stress?

Now, the very first thing I try to do is to avoid stressful situations in a whole, avoid people that may bring me stress. For example, toxic friends, toxic relationships, family members who like to gossip, and also not being at places where it doesn't fit my personality. For example, bars or clubs, those are not places that I would normally go to. If it's unavoidable and stress is at my door, what I try not to do is put other people's burden on top of me as well. Because if my cup is already full and someone comes and puts more on it, it's obviously going to overflow or I'm going to explode. And whenever I finish doing that, avoiding other people's burdens, I try to go into solitude, have time for myself, take a breath, relax, be in peace.

Whenever I'm comfortable talking about it, I may look to someone who I trust to confide in them, ask them for their advice to help me navigate through the situation. And last, I reflect. I try to reflect on what made me feel this way, what brought on the stress and how to avoid it, how to build a barrier around me or between this thing that brought me the stress. So that is what I do to manage.

And we do quite well, but it's not really about winning. When we do win, it's nice, but it's really just fun to be there with loads of other people having a good time and then just going home.

So quiz nights in my area are fun.

lessons.title: What is something that stresses me out?
lessons.description: One Minute English video lesson for Advanced learners.
lessons.transcriptHtml:
Hi, I'm Olivia. I'm originally from Washington DC, and right now I live in London. And my question is, what is something that stresses me out?

Unfortunately, I am prone to stress. I consider myself an anxious person. And because of that, I tend to plan and plan and plan ahead so that everything is in place and I've considered everything that can possibly go wrong and I've mapped out my day and I know how long it's going to take me. And I get really stressed out if other people don't adhere to the plan that I have in my head, which is a problem because I don't often communicate my plan because I'll just assume we're all on the same page about something. And then if the timing is slightly off or someone has a slightly different idea, I get really stressed out because I've built up all of my expectations on my own plan, and how that's going to go and I'm not very flexible to change.

So I'm really working on one, communicating what I have in my mind and two, not getting super anxious when plans change.

lessons.title: Does social media make people more happy or less happy?
lessons.description: One Minute English video lesson for Advanced learners.
lessons.transcriptHtml:
Hi, my name is Saif and I'm from Pakistan. And my question is, does social media make people more happy or less happy?

I believe that social media makes people happy for a limited time. And if the response is not continuous or prolonged, it makes people less happy. Social media presents a phenomena which combines happiness and sadness by way of likes, shares and comments. Thus, one's happiness or sadness is paramount on the number of hits your post receives. This way, a superficial ego bubble is created through social media, which the users strive to fill with active followers, and this makes them happy. Users conveniently share with the world only the exciting or the awe striking part of their lives. And the more the world likes their posts, the more they're happy.

lessons.title: Do you think AI or robots will be more harmful or helpful in the future?
lessons.description: One Minute English video lesson for Advanced learners.
lessons.transcriptHtml:
Hello, my name is Preah. My question was, do you think AI or robots will be more harmful or helpful in the future?

I am honestly not sure where I stand with this, so maybe you can help me out. I'm going to use a scenario to best explain how I feel about it. Let's talk about mobility and in the home. Let's say I'm a physically fit person and I have a robot that is able to cook, clean, wash, tidy up, do everything for me. All I need to do is just sit down, press a button or just say what I want it to do. I feel like if that will make people more lazier, less inclined to be physically active. And I think we will just be very dependent on robots to do everything for us. So I would say that is where the harm would come in in that aspect.

But let's think about the good or helpful. Let's talk about a person who isn't physically capable of doing things on their own or a person that is disabled. That would save them from having to hire a real life person to do these things for them if they had a robot to do it for them. But when you also think about the percentage of people who are physically incapable to the percentage of people that aren't physically incapable and can do things on their own, it would mean that it would be more harmful, wouldn't it?

  2. Becoming dependent on AI for moral choices is where the harm comes in.

physically incapable

lessons.title: Is it easy or hard to keep your appetite under control?
lessons.description: One Minute English video lesson for Advanced learners.
lessons.transcriptHtml:
Hi, my name is Maggie. I'm from the United States and my question was, is it easy or hard to keep your appetite under control?

For me, it depends. First of all, when I wake up in the morning and I walk into the kitchen and look in the fridge and I see all the food that is sitting in my fridge, immediately I get so hungry and I feel like I have to eat at that moment or the world is going to end if I do not eat right then. I also really like to snack and I really don't mind what I'm eating as long as I have something for a snack. The only thing I don't like is coconut, but I don't really know anyone who just snacks on coconut for fun. So that's okay. Whatever snack that I'm eating is perfect. However, sometimes when I'm working and I get distracted, I feel like I will forget to eat lunch sometimes just because I'm working and I'm not paying attention to the time.

But other than that, most of the time I definitely remember to eat because I'm hungry. So I'm curious, is it hard or easy for you to control your appetite?

Examples:

Meaning: Eats something as a snack (small food between meals).

Meaning: Not focused because something takes your attention away.

Examples:

  2. He was distracted by his phone during class.

Examples:

lessons.title: What is a rumor that you heard?
lessons.description: One Minute English video lesson for Advanced learners.
lessons.transcriptHtml:
Hi, I'm Olivia. I'm from Washington DC. Right now, I live in London. And my question is, what is a rumor that you heard?

Well, I'm going to share with you guys right now. So, I work in a retail store. I am not in any sort of management or leadership position, but I'm friends with a lot of the managers who are. And one of my friends who is one of the managers whispered to me three months ago, "Hey, I know that this bigger manager that people don't really like is quitting." But I wasn't allowed to say anything. So, she told me that she was quitting. I had to hide it. And a lot of my coworkers weren't happy with this manager. So, a couple people actually came forward and made an official complaint about this manager and tried to go to HR. And of course, the big bosses didn't do anything about it because they knew that this manager was quitting.

And I was the only one of my rank that knew that this manager was quitting. And then they were getting all upset that the big bosses weren't doing anything, and then I had to try and calm people down. But I guess, I don't know if it's a rumor if it's true. I guess it kind of is if it gets spread around. But yeah, I knew for about three months that one of my bosses that people didn't really like was quitting.

lessons.title: Do I like my role at my current job?
lessons.description: One Minute English video lesson for Advanced learners.
lessons.transcriptHtml:
Hi, my name is Tamara. I was born and raised in New York State in the United States. And right now I'm living in Ecuador, which is in South America. My question is, do I like my role at my current job?

Yes, I love my role at my current job, teaching English online to kids in China. Starting each class with basic conversations like asking students to share something good about their week or their day, what's their favorite thing about grandpa or grandma? It helps them transition from thinking in Chinese to speaking in English. This job helps me in tailoring activities for young and older students and introducing diverse themes such as nature and landmarks, to topics on brain activity and how it's used by scientists to discover new technologies. Creating a fun environment while encouraging participation keeps the students motivated and enhances their language development. Thus, I love being a part of their journey.

lessons.title: Have you had a job you hated?
lessons.description: One Minute English video lesson for Advanced learners.
lessons.transcriptHtml:
Hello, my name is Grace. I'm from South Africa, and a job I've had that I absolutely hated was cleaning squid.

So when I was younger, I volunteered at the aquarium, the Two Oceans Aquarium, for about a year. And I loved the job overall. I've been fortunate in that I've never worked at a place that I hated entirely. I always found something I enjoyed about the jobs I've done and the jobs I've been at. But cleaning squid to feed the animals, the aquarium was very important and very smelly. I really didn't enjoy it. I eventually had to get special clothes that I would only wear when I worked the back of house at the aquarium because I just couldn't get the smell out. And the squid, the insides, they would stain your clothes. It was terrible. However, I did enjoy parts of it. I got to feed turtles and penguins and I met interesting people.

I would not do the squid again though. Still, to this day, I hate it.

lessons.description: One Minute English video lesson for Advanced learners.
lessons.transcriptHtml:
Hello, my name is Elisabeth, and I am from the United States. And my question is, what is a movie that had really good acting?

So, I would definitely say a movie with really good acting is Forrest Gump. Now this movie, it starred Tom Hanks, Robin Wright, and it's excellent. Tom Hanks does a wonderful job performing a Southern accent. It is very convincing for someone who does not come from the South. Also characters like Lieutenant Dan, his mother, very convincing characters, also Robin Wright, who plays Jenny. You go through the movie feeling sorry for her, but also very frustrated with her sometimes with the way she acts towards Forrest.

But it's definitely a story. I'm always crying by the end of it, especially when Forrest has his little son, little Forrest. And yeah, it's just a wonderful example of acting done really well.

lessons.title: What is a company that went bankrupt?
lessons.description: One Minute English video lesson for Advanced learners.
lessons.transcriptHtml:
Hi, my name is Elizabeth and I'm from the United States. And my question is, what is a company that went bankrupt?

So one company that comes to mind is Toys "R" Us, and this was a huge toy retailer in the US, UK, several other countries. Now, this company went bankrupt in 2018. I used to love going to it as a kid. It had everything fun you could possibly imagine: games, balls, stuffed animals, Barbies, you name it. It was a kid paradise.

But the company really went bankrupt because of its inability to innovate or keep up with the times. So it really got taken over by companies like Amazon, Amazon Prime, as more people turn to online shopping and not an in-store experience. And also, I think it reflects that children today really aren't playing with physical toys. They're playing online video games, they're playing games on their phones. And yeah, again, Toys "R" Us just really went bankrupt because it just did not keep up with the changing times.

lessons.title: Do you think large charity organizations are effective?
lessons.description: One Minute English video lesson for Advanced learners.
lessons.transcriptHtml:
Hi, I'm Alias. I'm in the United States. And my question is, do you think large charity organizations are effective?

I admire large charity organizations for what they do. People had to start them, they had to fund them, and they have to have a mission that's beneficial to humankind. I think they are very effective in the people that they help. Charities have undoubtedly helped, if not millions of people, tens of millions, hundreds of millions.

However, they can't do the big work. They can't do the largest jobs. Society and politics and the way things are structured, government down, needs to be structured in a way that helps people the way that charities have been set up to do.

Charities are a temporary solution to permanent problems. Charities are admirable, but they will just continue to take money, funnel them into these things that need them. But society needs to be structured in a way that charities don't need to exist, to help people without the need for people to donate, without the need for charity.

lessons.title: What is a job that would stress you out?
lessons.description: One Minute English video lesson for Advanced learners.
lessons.transcriptHtml:
Hello, my name is Elizabeth. I am from the United States. And my question is, what is a job that would stress you out?

For me, being a nurse is a job that would be very stressful. I say this because I am very squeamish. I don't like the sight of blood or broken bones or anything gross. I also don't like the smell of a hospital, and I'm not very good in emergency situations. I tend to panic. I do not remain calm. So I don't think any patients would want me as their nurse. I do have friends who are very competent nurses. I'm very thankful that they are.

So, yes. So for me personally, this is not a job that I would want because again, I would be very stressed out.

Hello, my name is Tony. I'm from the UK. And my question is, what is a business that you would like to start?

Well, I am a huge and passionate fan of music and in particular live music, so I would love to open my own live music venue. I think it's really important for every city, every area to have a really vibrant local music scene. It's a really good creative place to be. I would invite bands from all over the country and, if I could, further afield, so any touring bands from other countries as well. Just good live music, all kinds of genres, four or five nights a week. And that would be my ultimate dream business.

lessons.title: Have you ever been someone's superior at work?
lessons.description: One Minute English video lesson for Advanced learners.
lessons.transcriptHtml:
Hello, my name is Chanel and I'm from the United States. And my question is, have you ever been someone's superior at work?

And the answer to that for me is yes. So when I was younger, I worked in a retail store. I was actually in my early twenties, so a lot of the individuals who worked under me were actually a lot older than me, and so this made for a very interesting experience for me being a superior at work.

Because of my age, sometimes I would have problems with some of the employees, so I had to be very stern, which is out of my character generally. Sometimes I had to do things I didn't want to do, be a little bit mean, but it was very important for me to stay on my ground a lot of times because I was someone superior at work.

So that was something that was a little bit uncomfortable for me, but it actually paid off in the long run. And it taught me a lot about managing and being fair but stern and getting the job done. So that was my experience of being someone superior at work. What about you? Have you ever been someone superior at work? Okay, until next time. Bye bye.

lessons.title: Should entrepreneurship be taught in schools?
lessons.description: One Minute English video lesson for Advanced learners.
lessons.transcriptHtml:
I'm Tahir, and I am from London in the United Kingdom. And my question is, should entrepreneurship be taught in schools?

I think that entrepreneurship should be a part of your school experience, but I'm not sure if we should necessarily spend an hour a day teaching entrepreneurship as a subject in and of itself.

So, for example, I know that in the US there were loads of fairs and competitions within the schools for different entrepreneurial related things like product designs or coming up with the best inventions, which I think is super cool. That's not really something that we have much of in the United Kingdom.

So I do think that entrepreneurship should be incorporated in the school culture, even if it's not directly taught as part of the everyday curriculum. So yeah, that's sort of my views on how entrepreneurship should have its role in day-to-day school learning.

lessons.title: Have you ever observed sketchy behavior?
lessons.description: One Minute English video lesson for Advanced learners.
lessons.transcriptHtml:
Hello, my name is Rocio, and I'm from El Salvador. My question is, have you ever observed sketchy behavior before?

And the answer is yes. There was this one time where I was at the mall waiting for a friend, and I remember that there was this man in front of me, maybe like five feet apart, that he was walking in circular motions. I wasn't really sure why. But he kept looking at me and I didn't really know why.

I had my headphones on, so I thought that maybe he wanted to sit down or maybe he just wanted to ask me something. So I removed my headphones and he never really said anything, but he just kept walking in circular motions and kept looking at me. I got really uncomfortable and then I just sort of left because he was really freaking me out.

Now, thankfully, it didn't really escalate to anything further. But yeah, I mean that was a pretty sketchy behavior that I sort of identified. lessons.title: Have you ever done multiple rounds of job interviews?
lessons.description: One Minute English video lesson for Advanced learners.
lessons.transcriptHtml:
Hi, I am Olivia. I'm from Washington D.C. And my question is, have you ever done multiple rounds of interviews for a job?

For a traditional job, no. That's typically like working retail or working as a barista behind the coffee counter. They're pretty simple jobs. They just need someone who's confident and has good communication skills. So I kind of do the one interview and we're fine.

But for an acting job, yes. And by interviews I might mean like a recall or a callback. So normally you submit your first self-tape, if they like you and they think you're a good fit for the role, they'll get back to you. And they'll either ask you to come in person, or they'll ask you to do a tape again with more scenes, or they'll give you critique. And then you send that in, or you attend the second round of auditions, and then sometimes they’ll ask you to come back again depending on how big the project is.

So there's been a few projects where I've gone back, I've gotten the role after two tries. There's a few projects where I've gone back three times. One of those I did get it and one of those I didn't get it. And it's good fun, it's good practice, but it is a bit annoying when you go for three or four rounds and then you don't end up getting it because you do get your hopes up. But it does just kind of depend on the job.

lessons.title: Who is a popular singer that you dislike?
lessons.description: One Minute English video lesson for Advanced learners.
lessons.transcriptHtml:
Hi, my name is Elizabeth. I am from the United States. And my question is, what is a popular singer that you dislike?

So, I would have to say a popular singer that I dislike is Taylor Swift. Now, I will say she has done a wonderful job marketing herself. She's very clever with writing song lyrics, and she puts on some impressive performances. But I just really don't understand the hype. I don't think that her song lyrics are very deep. I also think that her fan base, they like, no matter what song comes out, even if it's terrible, they're going to say that it is gold. Okay? So for those reasons, I don't really like her.

Now, I can quote some of her songs, especially her older country ones. So I do understand that she's very good at what she does, but for the reasons I mentioned, I just don't particularly like her.

lessons.title: What music is not your taste?
lessons.description: One Minute English video lesson for Advanced learners.
lessons.transcriptHtml:
Hello, my name is Chanel and I'm from the United States. And my question is, what kind of music is not your taste?

Well, for me, I don't really too much like rock music. Now, I'm not a big music person in general, but that is one genre of music that I'm not too fond of. When I do listen to music, I like it to have a certain beat, a certain rhythm, certain tempo. So a lot of times I like to sit and be laid-back and kind of just jam.

So the type of music that's not my taste will be rock. That's a little bit fast, faster paced, more loud. I can't really keep with the different rhythms and the timbres that it has going with it. So that is just not my style. When I have listened to rock before, it was more of a soft rock, a more… even had a little bit of an R&B type flair to it. So if I were to say that the music that is not my taste, it would be rock music.

What about you? What type of music is not your taste?

lessons.title: What movie had an ending that you hated?
lessons.description: One Minute English video lesson for Advanced learners.
lessons.transcriptHtml:
Hello, my name is Grace. I'm from South Africa, and what's a movie that had an ending that I hated?

I would say that would be 2001, A Space Odyssey. I think that movie is brilliant. It's fantastic and it's clever. It's beautiful, but I hate the ending. I know it's meant to be sort of difficult to understand, but it's not just difficult. It's also boring. Maybe it would've been more interesting if I'd seen it in the cinema and I wasn't from the era I'm from now. Some of the things are still really amazing, and I can watch some of the really long shots because they're gorgeous and some of the things really haven't come to pass. Some of them have, like,video calls, which is fascinating to see, but the ending goes on for so long and I really don't like it, and I think it spoils the whole film, but it's okay. You don't have to like every part of a movie, but that's one I really hate.

lessons.title: Have you ever dealt with racism or sexism?
lessons.description: One Minute English video lesson for Advanced learners.
lessons.transcriptHtml:
Hi, my name's Alejandro. I am from Toronto, Canada, and my question is, have you ever dealt with racism or sexism?

And I've dealt with both. Even being a man in the city, it's not uncommon. This is more so an easy question. Living in Canada as a person of color, racism isn't uncommon. While Canada's more accepting, given that we have a history of helping people escape slavery through the Underground Railroad in St. Catherine's, that doesn't mean everybody is so accepting, of course. Now, Toronto is a more multicultural city, but racism, again, it's not uncommon and hateful speech happens. I have worked as a tree planter, which has allowed me the privilege of traveling throughout so many wonderful different parts of Canada. And in these other parts of Canada, diversity is not as common, and people aren't always as familiar with other cultures, other cultural practices, and they're not as accepting. I've lived in places like Manitoba and Saskatchewan, and I definitely felt a little bit out of place, and that's okay. It's all a matter of how people kind of accept you into their communities, and they were still accepting, although there was different levels of discomfort that I felt and somewhat a little bit of familiar unfamiliarity on their part as to how other people interacted with me. So, there are different levels to this, but it happens in many different forms and it's not uncommon, but we strive. We strive, anyhow.

lessons.title: What worries you more the economy or the environment?
lessons.description: One Minute English video lesson for Advanced learners.
lessons.transcriptHtml:
Hi there. My name is Jerry. I'm from Cameron. The question is, what worries you more, the economy or the environment?

To me, I believe both because one inevitably affects the other. So, if we as a human race are able to build a more sustainable economy, a more efficient economy, we can in the long run build a more stable environment. For instance, planting new trees so that the sun rays doesn't hit the earth directly, or switching from gas-producing cars to electric cars, switching from electric power stations to solar panels. These are sufficient and world-renowned renewable energies that can in the long run make our ecosystem more preferable. If you cut down trees and you keep using pollution-driven industries and cars, the ecosystem will be worn out, allowing the sun rays to directly heat the earth. In the long run, it will cause drought, it will cause famine, and the whole economy and the environment itself will all suffer. So, I believe if we take care of our economy, we will in the long run take care of our environment.

lessons.title: Have you ever had a big break that changed your life?
lessons.description: One Minute English video lesson for Advanced learners.
lessons.transcriptHtml:
Hi, my name is Lillian and I'm answering the question, have you ever had a big break or really fortunate event that changed your life?

And yes, I had one. Because of my good grades in school, I was able to obtain a scholarship to Estoria, one of the best schools in my country. And as a result, I met the US Ambassador in my country. It was a wonderful opportunity for me because thanks to the relationship that my school had with the scholarship program from the US Embassy, I was also able to get certified as a professional translator through another scholarship.

And, I also got my visa to work in the US if I wanted to in the future. So, to be honest, I never thought I would have that opportunity. But since I started studying, I have had good results always. So, I can say that I do not regret at all always giving my best in all my projects.

lessons.title: Do you have deadlines at your job?
lessons.description: One Minute English video lesson for Advanced learners.
lessons.transcriptHtml:
Hello, my name is Chanel, and I am from the United States, and my question is, do you have deadlines at your job?

Well, for me, I have two jobs. So, my first job is that I'm a stay-at-home mom who home-schools, and the second job that I have, I am a self-published author. So, for my first job, I set my own deadlines. So, I set deadlines that work best for me to make sure I get everything done around the home, and then also to make sure my kiddos stay on track and learn everything that they need to learn. For my second job as being a self-published author, sometimes I still am making my own deadlines, since I'm not going through a publishing company. But I do have to make sure I make deadlines for the printer, for advertising and for things like that to make sure that I have everything flowing well with the book. Now for those deadlines, for working with people that's outside of my own little self-publishing bubble. Those deadlines, yes, I have to make sure that I follow to make sure everything gets out and goes to the printer, and everything happens on time, but I do like the stay-at-home mom side of things to where I can be a little bit lax on my deadlines. So, I have the best of both worlds. What about you? Does your job have deadlines that you have to follow?

lessons.title: Who is someone you can count on?
lessons.description: One Minute English video lesson for Advanced learners.
lessons.transcriptHtml:
Hi, my name is Elizabeth and I am from the United States, and my question is, who is someone you can count on?

So, I know that I could count on my mom, for example, my dad or my sister. If something was wrong, I know I could call them up and they'd be there. But someone outside of family that I know I can count on is my friend William. He is always helping others. For example, this past weekend, my sister-in-law had a flat tire. We called him. He immediately came and fixed it.

A few weeks ago, another friend was moving and he cleared his schedule for the weekend to ensure that he could help him move into his new house, picking up heavy furniture and lending his truck. I also know, for example, if I'm upset about something, I could call him up and he would listen. So he's definitely the kind of friend that you want to have. He's always giving, always helping, and I know that I can count on him.

Meaning: The wife of your brother or the sister of your spouse.

ensure

Meaning: To make certain that something happens or is done.

Examples:

  1. Double-check the address to ensure the package gets delivered correctly.
  2. He worked overtime to ensure the project was finished on time.

be there

Examples:

  2. She promised they’d be there to help set up for the event.

  2. My town has no stores outside of a few shops.

lessons.title: What would you change about the education system?
lessons.description: One Minute English video lesson for Advanced learners.
lessons.transcriptHtml:
Hello, I'm Victoria from Suriname, and my question is, what would you change about the educational system in your country?

Well, there are many things that need to be changed in my country regarding the educational system, but I would start with two things. The first one is teachers pay. In the whole Caribbean, the wages in my country for teachers is the second lowest, which is actually very bad and very saddening. Because of this, many teachers either leave the country or have side hustles, which is understandable and consciously or unconsciously, this will undoubtedly affect the quality of our profession, so rewarding teachers for their important role is a great motivator.

Secondly, I would invest in ICT because learning and 21st century skills go hand in hand now, but the situation is very bad. So, access to these modern technologies is limited, which affects the way we teach and the way we learn, so I would really invest in ICT and teacher pay to begin with.

Examples:

lessons.title: What industry will AI put out of business?
lessons.description: One Minute English video lesson for Advanced learners.
lessons.transcriptHtml:
Hello, my name is Grace. I'm from South Africa. And what industry will AI put out of business?

I don't know. I don't think anyone knows enough to definitively say that AI will put a specific industry out of business. It's a bit like saying AI will put sort of paper-based media out of business, even though if anything happens to paper-based media, that'll be because of the times changing, not because of artificial intelligence, but just technology as a whole. And it's a bit like saying, you know, the telephone industry has been put out of business, and it's not. Even though you used to have operators who would reroute calls and those jobs became obsolete, the technology changed, but the simple fact of contacting people and needing to be in contact with other people remained.

And I think at the heart of it, some of the needs that industries have seen to and taken care of will still be there. So, in some form, the industry will exist, but there will be lots of changes because of AI, at least.

  2. We need to consider the system as a whole, rather than focusing on one issue.

Meaning: Used to compare one idea to another in order to explain or make a point.

Examples:

  2. Criticizing all employees for one mistake is a bit like saying the whole team is incompetent.

Examples:

  2. You can’t ignore the simple fact that exercise improves health.

Meaning: Referring to the core or most important aspect of something.

Examples:

Meaning: To cause a company or industry to close down or stop operating.

  2. If they can’t keep up with new trends, the company might be put out of business.

obsolete

Meaning: No longer used or needed because it has been replaced by something newer.

Examples:

  1. Typewriters have become obsolete with the invention of computers.
  2. Some jobs may become obsolete as technology advances.

lessons.title: Do we live in a dog-eat-dog world?
lessons.description: One Minute English video lesson for Advanced learners.
lessons.transcriptHtml:
Hi, my name is Billy, and today I will be talking about, do you think or do I think that we live in a dog-eat-dog world?

So just to start off, the definition of a dog-eat-dog world is a world in which people will do anything to be famous or to be successful, even if it means hurting other people.

Now, although I will say that the world has shifted with hurting people in a way, I think that people are trying to help each other. However, we still live in such a world.

People will do anything for their, what we call, 60 seconds or 30 seconds of fame. And even if it means revealing something embarrassing about a friend, a family, a boss, a coworker, a past lover, or even a girlfriend or boyfriend at the moment, they will do it. Anything they can do to be on, what we call, that 30 seconds of fame.

And with that friendship are hurt, relationships and trust are broken. And this for me is still an indication that we live in a dog-eat-dog world.

lessons.title: What is a sign of the times?
lessons.description: One Minute English video lesson for Advanced learners.
lessons.transcriptHtml:
Hi, I'm Olivia. I'm originally from Washington DC and right now I live in London. And my question is, what is something that is a sign of the times?

For me, it's the video and the whole trend, tube girl. I dunno if you guys have seen it, but basically it's this girl who's recording herself on the tube dancing and singing, and there's a bunch of wind blowing in her face, and the dance is quite brave. It's not something I would want to do in public. And everybody in the background's watching her. And of course it went viral because of how shocking it was. And then because of that, she got lots of work and now there's all these videos you see of her in public having a phone and all these different angles and it looks really, really, really cool on the video camera, but it looks really stupid when you watch it live in public.

And you see her doing this around a bunch of stars at really important events, at fashion shows and seeing how stupid she looked in real life. But how cool the videos looked on her phone made me think of, wow, it really shows, it's a sign of the times that how you look online is now so much more important than how you look on real life because people place so much weight on your online presence. And that's something that's changed only recently. It was never like this before, that people care more about their online image than their in-person image. So, that's what I think is a sign of the times.

lessons.title: Are poor people happier than rich people?
lessons.description: One Minute English video lesson for Advanced learners.
lessons.transcriptHtml:
Hello, I'm Victoria and I'm from Suriname. My question is, do you think poor people are happier than rich people?

I believe this is a very difficult question to answer because the question contains some generalizations. Poor people, and rich people are lumped together here, and they are compared as a group, which I think is not entirely accurate because you have different types of poor people. You have poor people that are content with what they have or don't have, and when you are content, it contributes to your happiness.

Whereas there are poor people that are not happy with their circumstances, understandably so, because let's take for example, people who live in famine-stricken areas or areas with natural disasters that have robbed them of everything they have, their homes, their livelihood, their security, healthcare. I mean, it is understandable that people become unhappy if they have to suffer.

On the other hand, you have rich people. I think there are a number of types of rich people. You have rich people that are never satisfied, keep chasing more and more and more, and those people tend to be unhappy. Whereas there might be rich people who have purpose and are content with what they have, which contributes to their happiness. So, I think it really depends on what type of poor people are being compared to what type of rich people.

lumped together

Meaning: Grouped into one category without considering differences.

Examples:

content

Meaning: Satisfied and happy with what you have.

Examples:

  2. Being content with your life doesn’t mean you can’t work toward new goals.

famine-stricken

Meaning: Severely affected by a lack of food.

  2. Many families in famine-stricken areas struggle to survive each day.

robbed

Meaning: Taken away by force or circumstance.

Examples:

  2. She felt robbed of her happiness after losing her job.

livelihood

Meaning: The way someone earns money or resources to live.

  2. The storm destroyed crops, affecting the farmers’ livelihoods.

lessons.title: What personal info is none of people's business?
lessons.description: One Minute English video lesson for Advanced learners.
lessons.transcriptHtml:
Hello, my name is Grace. I'm from South Africa, and what personal info do I think is no one else's business?

I would say having children. I love kids, and it doesn't mean that everyone's going to have kids, and some people don't like kids, and they will have children, but I think putting the pressure on people, especially if you see a couple together and you go, right, when are you having children? Or just asking someone because of their age if they're going to have children. I'm fortunate in that I don't really get that question a lot, but I do think it's something personal, that it's not just something you do. It's not like going to the shop to buy some milk. It's not like just getting a pet. That's a big responsibility, but you know you're going to outlive your pet, your child will be your responsibility, your connection, someone that you're connected to for the rest of your life. It's not something that's mentioned or should be mentioned in just really casual conversation with acquaintances.

So, yeah, I would say that's something that's none of people's business.

lessons.title: Do you have a timeframe for your goals?
lessons.description: One Minute English video lesson for Advanced learners.
lessons.transcriptHtml:
Hi, I am Olivia. I'm from Washington, DC and right now I live in London. And my question is, do I have a timeframe for my future goals?

And the answer is yes. Part of the reason is because I live in London. My visa depends on me making certain career goals by a certain time. Otherwise, I'm unable to stay in this country. So, I'm an actor, and what that means is I have to perform in a certain amount of professional productions, whether that be through theater or film and TV in a certain amount of countries in order to get my next visa. And that for me expires in about a year and a half.

So I have a year and a half to do maybe one professional production here in the UK, maybe one professional production somewhere else. Hopefully somewhere that pays well, maybe someplace like Germany. And all of those productions have to have a certain number of credentials and reviews. So, yes, I have a year and a half to start supporting myself as an actor so that I can stay living and working in London, which is what I would really like to do.

lessons.title: What are your thoughts about gentrification?
lessons.description: One Minute English video lesson for Advanced learners.
lessons.transcriptHtml:
Hi, my name is Billy, and I am currently living in South Africa, and today I will be talking about what are my thoughts about gentrification.

So, basically the definition of gentrification is when a maybe rundown area or well-known poor area suddenly becomes more modern or filled with rich people, because now the rich people are moving into that area, maybe to invest or to build bigger houses and such. So, what ends up happening most of the time is that poor people who have been in that area usually have to be displaced or they have to move.

Now, my thoughts about this is that it comes with its pros and its cons, for example, the reputation of an area. If the area is known to be more of a poorer area and maybe the government wants to remove that or to change that reputation, I think that would be a good plan.

However, the con to this is that it would be really sad that families who have lived here for, in that area, sorry, for many, many years, and now they're suddenly asked to move because the prices of rent or just living in that area has increased now that there is growth, sudden growth and interest in the area. I think if you are thinking of moving to a certain area, you should be considerate of the people who have lived there, and who have started calling that place home. So, although it benefits the economy and it benefits the housing industry, it doesn't always benefit the citizens.

lessons.title: What is something you need to work on?
lessons.description: One Minute English video lesson for Advanced learners.
lessons.transcriptHtml:
Hi, my name is Elizabeth. I'm from the United States, and my question is, what is something you need to work on?

Something that I personally need to work on is not interrupting when other people are speaking. So, I have noticed many times when I am in a conversation with a family member or a friend, they'll be speaking, sharing a story, for example, and I will jump in with what I want to say and interrupt them, which is very rude. Something that I'm trying to work on is actively listening to what the other person is saying, waiting until they finished their thought or their story, and then saying what it is that I wanted to say.

This is difficult for me because I have many thoughts running through my head. I'm worried that I'll forget what it is that I was going to say, but again, interrupting is very rude. It's impolite to the other person. So, I'm working on, again, actively listening and not interrupting the other person.

  2. She jumped in to help when she saw her friend struggling with the heavy box.

work on

Meaning: To put effort into improving something or completing a task.

Examples:

  1. I need to work on my pronunciation to sound more natural in English.
  2. He is working on a project about climate change for his science class.

Meaning: Stopping someone from speaking by saying or doing something before they finish.

  2. Before the big exam, I had so many thoughts running through my head about what I needed to study.

but again

Meaning: A phrase used to repeat or emphasize an idea that has already been mentioned.

Examples:

  1. I really like ice cream, but again, it’s not very healthy if I eat it every day.
  2. I’m sorry I’m late, but again, the traffic was terrible this morning.
